About-C.dc.html.What: Governance as a real reading experience — the bylaws are the official web text with a sticky contents rail, "In plain words" summaries, redlines that show exactly what each vote changed, a per-version change log, a searchable minutes archive (matching sentence shown in the row) and a new Decisions register that indexes every motion and links it to its minutes and the section it changed; email subscription for governance updates.
About-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: Chicago Councilmatic (searchable decisions, plain summaries, subscribe), Keep a Changelog (Added/Changed/Removed/Fixed per version), NN/g (web page first, PDF as a download; "Last updated" stamps).
About-C.dc.html.Trade-off: The secretary has to enter motions and section versions in a structured way after each meeting instead of uploading one PDF; if that slips, the register and change log go stale.
About-C.dc.html.Build notes: New D1 tables gov_versions (document, version, adopted_at, motion_id), gov_sections (version_id, number, title, body_html, plain_summary), gov_motions (number, meeting_id, text, topic, result, vote, affects_section) and gov_subscribers, plus an FTS5 index over minutes/bylaws/rules; Pages Functions /api/governance/{versions,diff,search,motions,subscribe}; extend GovLayout/BylawsPage/MinutesPage (sticky TOC, redline via jsdiff, PDF generated from the HTML) and give GovernanceDocuments a section-by-section editor beside RichTextEditor; Resend emails subscribers when minutes or a version is published.

About-D.dc.html.What: A living heritage page — a Reigning champions band (the same data feeds a one-line homepage band), an honor roll filtered by title with "Show all N years" and player pages behind every name, a single timeline from Morphy's birth (1837) through LCA's 1915 start to Sulphur 2026 beside a step-through Opera Game board, and a "Help fill the gaps" drive that shows record coverage by decade and lets members send crosstables, photos and clippings into a review queue.
About-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: North Carolina Chess Association and Irish Chess Union (current-champions band, filterable champions table by year and title, "Show all N years"), Irish Chess Union (champion rows linking to full results).
About-D.dc.html.Trade-off: Most of the value depends on someone digitising old records and moderating submissions; until the archive grows, many rows and timeline points stay as gaps (which the page shows openly rather than hiding).
About-D.dc.html.Build notes: Extend champions (migration 0049: year, title, champion, notes, linked event) with player_id, section, rating, score, city, co_champion flag, and add history_submissions (year, event, kind, files in R2, submitter, status) plus a players table that links champions and registrations by US Chess ID; Pages Functions /api/champions?title=&year=, /api/players/:id, /api/history/submissions (R2 upload + officer review in ChampionsPanel); on finalize of an event with is_state_championship, propose the standings winner to ChampionsPanel; new HomePage ChampionsBand, ChampionsPage honor roll and a small PGN stepper (chess.js) for the Opera Game with a lichess link.

Member-A.dc.html.What: Eligibility first. Two yes/no questions, then a household builder that prices every combination (Family vs Adult/Senior + Scholastic), recommends the cheapest and prints the family math openly ("Family only saves with three children"). All four tiers sit below with the fitting one highlighted. Join and Renew are separate paths (renewal by emailed link), plus an "Am I a member?" lookup, gift memberships, an optional home club, and pay first / set a password after.
Member-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: USA Pickleball and AMNH (separate Join and Renew paths, tiers described by who they cover), Patreon (one highlighted tier, labelled "Fits your answers" because "Most popular" isn't known to be true), Irish Chess Union (buying memberships for others), NN/g and Smashing pricing guidance (say who each option is for).
Member-A.dc.html.Trade-off: The questions add a step for people who already know they want Adult, so the plain tier cards must stay one click away. The optimizer's rules (ties, seniors, up to 3 children, adding a child later) must match board policy exactly, or the "honest math" stops being honest.
Member-A.dc.html.Build notes: Add a household quote function to pricing.ts (inputs: senior flag, children with is_k12) and new membership fields home_club_id, gift_code, recipient_email, claimed_at. Pages Functions: /api/membership/quote; /api/membership/lookup (US Chess ID or email returns first name, last initial, tier, status and expiry; rate-limited); /api/membership/renew-link (Resend magic link); and a guest Stripe Checkout whose MembershipSuccessPage creates the account and sets the password. Reuse family.ts/FamilyCard for children without logins and UscfSearchInput for ID matching.

Member-B.dc.html.What: A conventional, easy-to-scan pricing page built on honest numbers: four tier cards described by who they cover, one highlight with a label that is literally true ("Best value with 3 children") and the family math printed on the card. Below that: "What your dues fund" (treasurer placeholders plus a link to the report); membership that takes care of itself (opt-in auto-renew, reminders 30 and 7 days out, a lapse check inside registration, gift memberships); a home-club member count; and an FAQ that opens with "LCA vs US Chess".
Member-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: Patreon (single highlighted tier), AMNH and USA Pickleball (tiers by who's covered, Renew next to Join), NN/g and Smashing pricing-page guidance (same attributes on every card, say who each is for, no hidden costs), NN/g nonprofit study (say where the money goes).
Member-B.dc.html.Trade-off: Less guided than Member-A, so visitors still pick the tier themselves. The dues breakdown is only credible once the treasurer enters real figures. Auto-renew brings Stripe subscription upkeep (failed cards, cancellations, refunds).
Member-B.dc.html.Build notes: Stripe Billing subscriptions for opt-in auto-renew (membership.auto_renew, stripe_subscription_id, plus webhook handling in functions/api/stripe). The daily-emails Worker cron sends the 30- and 7-day reminders and pre-charge notices through Resend with signed renew links. RegisterPage and pricing.ts compare membership expiry with the event date and offer a renewal line item. Add membership.home_club_id, with member counts on ClubDetailPage and a renewals list in ManageClubPage. Dues categories come from a treasurer-edited finance_summary table linked to the treasurer-report document. MembershipPage is rebuilt as cards plus FAQ.

Member-C.dc.html.What: A purpose-first /donate page. The donor picks one of three funds ("Send a Louisiana kid to Nationals", "Club equipment", "General fund"), each with its goal and progress, then fills a short sticky form: once or monthly, four amounts plus Other (numeric keypad), a board-approved impact line, cover-the-fee, tribute gift and an opt-in name, then Stripe Checkout. Also on the page: a money-in/money-out table per fund linked to the treasurer's report, plus four trust facts; sponsored entries, which turn gifts into scholastic entry fees that families request privately at registration; one optional add-on at every LCA checkout; an opt-in thank-you wall; other ways to give, including a December appeal.
Member-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: GiveDirectly and Wikimedia (plain framing, amount buttons, a trust fact up front), NN/g nonprofit study (say where donations go; only 4% do), Baymard (a visibly secure payment step), M+R Benchmarks (monthly giving, December appeal), North Carolina Chess Association (entry-fee assistance program).
Member-C.dc.html.Trade-off: Fund accounting is ongoing work. The treasurer must log spending per fund for the table and progress bars to stay true, an officer has to review sponsored-entry requests before each event, and restricted funds limit how the board can spend the money.
Member-C.dc.html.Build notes: New D1 tables funds (name, goal, season, active), donations (fund_id, amount, frequency, Stripe ids, show_name, tribute), fund_disbursements (fund_id, amount, note, date) and sponsored_entry_requests (registration_id, status, approved_by). Pages Functions: /api/donations/checkout (Stripe Checkout in payment or subscription mode), /api/donations/funds (totals and progress), /api/donations/wall, plus the webhook in functions/api/stripe. A new DonatePage puts the unused DonateButton in the header, footer, confirmation pages and ScholasticPage. RegisterPage gets "Request a sponsored entry" and the optional add-on, with officer review in AdminPage. Resend sends receipts and "your gift covered N entries" updates.

Member-D.dc.html.What: One membership card in four places (Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes with front and back, a My LCA card with a pass per child, printable member and family cards) sharing one signed QR that checks people in at the director's table or by scanning the door poster; on event days the pass shows round, board and color.
Member-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: Apple Wallet pass layout (header/primary/secondary/auxiliary fields, contact info on the back, navy-and-gold sample), Delta + Apple "Add to Wallet" membership block, CaissaChess barcode ID cards, Tabroom check-in sheets, Chesstide door poster with QR.
Member-D.dc.html.Trade-off: The heaviest membership option to run: Apple passes need a paid Apple Developer account plus signing and push certificates, and event-day pass updates need a pass web service. Paper and the in-account card cover anyone who skips the wallet.
Member-D.dc.html.Build notes: New tables wallet_passes (member_id, platform, serial, auth_token, push_token, updated_at) and checkin_tokens (HMAC-signed member token); Pages Functions /api/membership/card.pkpass (passkit-generator), /api/membership/google-wallet (Google Wallet API "Save to Wallet" JWT), the PassKit web-service routes (/api/passes/v1/devices…, /passes/…) for updates, and /api/membership/card.pdf (replaces the Apps Script; sent as a Resend attachment). New MemberCard component (front/back toggle, per-child passes, full-screen QR) on DashboardPage; family.ts supplies the children; the TD console's camera scan verifies the token against a cached entry list, so it works offline.

Account-A.dc.html.What: "Next up" dashboard for an adult member (Avery): a Needs-attention row (unpaid entry before the early-entry deadline, US Chess membership ending before an entered event, LCA membership ending in 21 days), then one date-ordered timeline that mixes entries, saved events (LCA and partner), deadlines and the home club's nights, each entry carrying a Registered, Paid, Pairings posted, Results tracker; side column with wallet card, US Chess status, alert preferences (text/email), a personal calendar feed and count-up milestones; history table and settings below.
Account-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: NN/g + Baymard (current status and next action first; tracker), KingRegistration (US Chess expiry flagged against the event date), Delta SkyMiles (membership block with progress and "Add to Wallet"), parkrun + Peloton milestones (events and volunteering, no streak pressure), Luma / start.gg reminders before events.
Account-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Showing saved events and club nights alongside entries makes a long page for active players, and the nightly US Chess check depends on lookups that can be slow or rate-limited.
Account-A.dc.html.Build notes: New tables saved_events (member_id, tournament_id or clearinghouse_id, entered_elsewhere flag), member_alert_prefs (channel per alert type) and member_milestones (or a view over registrations + volunteer roles); a cron Worker that re-checks US Chess expiry for members with upcoming entries (functions/api/uscf lookup) and writes flags; /api/me/next-up (merges registrations, saved events, deadlines, club meeting rules), /api/me/calendar.ics (tokenized feed), SMS via a new Twilio integration next to Resend. DashboardPage rebuilt from NeedsAttention, NextUpTimeline, EntryStatusTracker and MilestoneBars components, plus the MemberCard from Member-D.

Account-B.dc.html.What: Parent-first dashboard for Danielle: household header with everyone's chips, two needs-attention items (Leo has no US Chess ID before his first event; Maya's bye waiting on the director), one card per person (next events, section, payment, US Chess status, kid-sized milestone; an empty state for the parent with a next step), a live Family day view that lays both kids' rounds side by side (board, color, result, "Playing now", text when each round pairs), a one-payment "Register the family" checkout with suggested sections and checkbox eligibility, Family-plan seats with an honest price check, guardian invites, Add a child (name, optional US Chess ID, "In 8th grade or below?") and family results.
Account-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: AskFRED / Chess67 / onlineregistration.cc "Who's playing?" household picker, ChessRoster (one section panel per player, one fee table, one payment), Eventbrite per-attendee checkout with an eligibility checkbox, Chess67 / start.gg / melee.gg "Your board" card (round, board, color) for the live day view, parkrun junior milestones (first, 5th, 10th), AMNH family tier that names who's covered, NN/g empty states with a next step.
Account-B.dc.html.Trade-off: The day view only shines on event days and needs pairings published through the site in real time; the rest of the year it is a preview, and the page is long for families with three kids.
Account-B.dc.html.Build notes: Extends family.ts children (no logins) with optional uscf_id and an eligibility_confirmations row per entry (section + checkbox, no grade); new guardians table (account_id, child_id, role) for co-parents; /api/me/household (people, entries, membership seats), /api/registrations/household-checkout (one Stripe Checkout Session with a line item per player; reuses pricing.ts member pricing and sectionRules.ts suggestions), /api/me/day-view?date= (round, board, color, result per child from pairings) plus SMS on pairing publish. Components: FamilyCard and FamilyRegistrationPanel reworked into PersonCard, FamilyDayView, HouseholdCheckout; UscfSearchInput for "Look up by name"; GradeConfirm for the checkbox.

Account-C.dc.html.What: One login, many roles (Chris: member, parent, club rep, tournament director, board rep) with no mode switch: role chips at the top name every role and jump to its section; a single "Today across your roles" list merges tasks with a worded role label (US Chess expiries among entrants, a bye request to approve, a board vote, the club freshness check, a child's unpaid entry, board inbox); then sections per role: You (with directing and volunteering milestones), Family, Your club (line-by-line "Is this still accurate?" with Confirm all, page stats, quick actions), Events you direct (X of Y by section, flags, setup checklist, Event-day console link, rating-report check on a finished club night), Board (inbox preview, open vote, meetings, drafts). Left rail: section counts, shortcuts into Workspace, a daily-digest toggle.
Account-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: NN/g on personalization and modes (accurate role-based sections, no switcher), GOV.UK task list (status in words), ChessRoster registrations grid + Chesstide/ChessRoster setup checklist, Chess67 checks before the rating report, KingRegistration director-only US Chess expiry flags, parkrun volunteer milestones, Peloton milestone counts.
Account-C.dc.html.Trade-off: The page grows with every role, so a heavy volunteer gets a long scroll; the merged Today list needs careful ranking or one role's noise drowns the rest.
Account-C.dc.html.Build notes: roles.ts already returns a user's roles; add role_assignments (user_id, role, scope_type club/tournament/board_seat, scope_id, starts_on, ends_on, granted_by) for scoped roles and co-director/co-rep delegation with dates; /api/me/tasks aggregates per-role task providers (registrations flags, bye requests, club freshness, governance votes, board inbox counts, unpaid family entries) into one ranked list; club_freshness (club_id, field, confirmed_at, confirmed_by) drives the "still accurate?" prompt (a cron Worker nags after 6 months); a daily-digest template on the existing daily-emails Worker. Components: RoleChips, TodayList, RoleSection wrappers over existing ManageClubPage, TournamentList, UsChessUploadPanel and BoardInboxPage data.

Work-A.dc.html.What: Tablet-first event-day console for the TD (The Baton Rouge Classic, Sun 9:14 AM before round 4): navy status band with a countdown, a round rail (check-in, rounds 1–5, prizes, rating report) and an offline/sync badge; a "Next step" strip that gates one big button at a time (confirm the disputed round-3 board, pair round 4 with a choice for no-shows, then publish and notify everyone in one tap); a round check-in list with big 52px actions, counts, search, filter chips and live scan sources (wallet card at the desk, door QR, TD tap), plus undo; a touch results grid (1–0 / ½–½ / 0–1 buttons, result source tags, keyboard 1/2/3, players reporting from their phones with mismatches flagged); print and QR outputs, an announcement composer (text, email, hall TV, banner) with a sent log, and a rating-report pre-check.
Work-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Chesstide (per-round check-in badges with undo, 1/2/3 + arrow result entry, "Check-in All", event poster with QR, pairing sheets labeling pairing bye 1 / requested ½ / absent 0), Chess67 (checks before the rating report, offline mode, player results kiosk), ChessRoster (results by link or text reply, provisional until the director confirms), CaissaChess (barcode ID cards, full-screen hall view), KingRegistration (director-only US Chess expiry flags), start.gg (check-in countdown).
Work-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Real-time sync plus offline editing is the hardest engineering on this board (two tablets editing the same round need conflict rules), texting players costs money per message, and player-reported results need a dispute flow TDs trust.
Work-A.dc.html.Build notes: New tables round_checkins (tournament_id, round, player_id, status here/bye/absent/withdrawn, method desk/scan/door_qr/self, at, by), result_reports (pairing_id, reporter_id, result, at) feeding a provisional/confirmed state on pairings, announcements (tournament_id, audience, channels, body, sent_at, counts). Pages Functions: /api/tournaments/:id/checkin (verifies Member-D's signed token), /rounds/:n/pair (existing Swiss engine), /rounds/:n/publish (fan-out: Resend email, Twilio SMS, wallet-pass push, hall-TV channel), /report-check (expired IDs, bye limits, missing results), /api/me/report-result for players; live updates via a Durable Object (or short polling), offline via a service worker + IndexedDB queue. New EventDayConsole route under WorkspacePage built from NextStepPanel, CheckInList, ResultsGrid (touch replacement for ResultsEntry's wide table), AnnouncementComposer and ReportCheck; reuses TournamentPrintPage outputs and UsChessUploadPanel; splits today's 5-tab TournamentManagePage so setup stays there and event day lives here.

Clubs-A.dc.html.What: List and map side by side with lettered pins linked to the rows. Each row starts with when the club meets and a computed "Tonight" or next date, then name, venue and tags. Day and "Good for" chips filter list and pins together, and every row shows a Confirmed stamp or a Needs-check flag. The 7 clubs with no schedule sit in their own honest group, each with an "Add their times" link.
Clubs-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Baymard (map beside the list), NC Chess Association (Last confirmed + Report outdated info), Seattle tags (quick filter chips), Downriver (honest venue types), Google advanced markers + clustering, W3C/WCAG 2.5.7 (list as the map's text alternative, zoom buttons)
Clubs-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Every club needs a structured schedule and a confirmed date before the page works, and 25 rows make a long page at 1440px (about 2600px tall).
Clubs-A.dc.html.Build notes: D1 migration adds `club_meetings` (club_id, weekday, start/end time, recurrence weekly|nth:"1,3,5"|monthly|seasonal, venue, notes), `clubs.last_confirmed_at` and `clubs.tags` (rated, casual, kids, beginners, free, venue_type). GET /api/clubs returns next_meeting (lcaTime.ts) and POST /api/clubs/:id/report emails the club_rep via Resend, escalating to admin after 14 days. ClubsPage adds day/good-for chips, sort and Near me (geolocation). LCAMap moves to AdvancedMarkerElement with letter glyphs + MarkerClusterer and two-way hover/selection. Per-club .ics comes from functions/api/clubs/[id]/ics.

Clubs-B.dc.html.What: A statewide Monday–Sunday timetable of all 19 real meetings this week, with days as columns and morning/afternoon/evening as rows. A navy "Tonight" panel with a small map of tonight's clubs comes first. Region pills count this week's meetings, and repeat rules handle 1st/3rd/5th-week, monthly and summer-only clubs (Bluebonnet's skipped Sunday, Picayune's rated 1st Monday). The weekend's Lafayette Open sits in the grid, and a club-rep panel shows the schedule editor and the 90-day "still accurate?" email.
Clubs-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: Saint Louis, Columbia and Downriver (statewide weekly grid; Downriver's real "no play on Saints game nights" skip rule), Seattle tags (Tonight and quick filters), NC Chess Association (freshness loop), parkrun (newcomers need "when do you meet" first)
Clubs-B.dc.html.Trade-off: Clubs without a structured schedule (7 not listed, plus 3 monthly or seasonal) drop off the grid into side lists, and the 8-column table scrolls sideways on phones, where the Tonight panel does most of the work.
Clubs-B.dc.html.Build notes: `club_meetings` (as in Clubs-A) plus `club_meeting_exceptions` (date, off|moved, note). GET /api/clubs/week?start= expands occurrences server-side (lcaTime.ts, America/Chicago) and merges Louisiana events from tournaments + clearinghouse. ICS feeds come from functions/api/calendar/clubs.ics?region=… and per club. New ClubWeekGrid + TonightPanel components go on ClubsPage, with a home "Play tonight" strip. The daily-emails Worker cron sends 90-day confirm emails with signed one-click links (POST /api/clubs/:id/confirm) and sets needs_check after 30 days, notifying the regional rep.

Clubs-C.dc.html.What: The 7 official regions as sections, each with a mini-map cropped to its clubs, its board seat (a rep with a Message button, or "Seat open · Volunteer", which also flags listings that need a check), its clubs with meeting lines, and its upcoming tournaments. "Find my region", region chips with counts, an overview map, per-region "Get updates" emails and a Start-a-club card come with it.
Clubs-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: NC Chess Association (region chips with counts, cards grouped by region, clubs keep their own entries), Michigan and Texas (regional reps as cards, open seats labeled), Colorado "Add Club" and Mississippi Scholastic (start a club / host an event), NC freshness loop (checked stamps)
Clubs-C.dc.html.Trade-off: All 25 clubs must be assigned to a region first (blank in live data) and reps recruited. People near a border (Hammond, Picayune) may look in the wrong section, and cross-region questions like "who meets Tuesday?" are harder than in A or B.
Clubs-C.dc.html.Build notes: Backfill clubs.region (regions.ts) in AdminClubPage. Board seats get region + vacancy (BoardSeatsPanel). GET /api/regions returns club counts, the rep or vacancy, a last-checked date and upcoming events (tournaments + clearinghouse via a city→region map). New `region_subscriptions` (email, region, token) gets a daily-emails Worker digest when clubs or events are added. "Find my region" uses browser geolocation + a static parish→region GeoJSON lookup. New RegionSection component: a small LCAMap per region with fitBounds, plus a rep card that opens a relay message form (no public emails).

Club-B.dc.html.What: A club-branded mini-site for Baton Rouge Chess Club. It has a colour band and tint, a logo slot, Follow and Add to calendar, and a "Next at the club" card built from both weekly nights. Anchor tabs lead to About (two ways to play, first-visit Q&A, a two-venue map, facts), Events (club events registered on LCA with X of Y counts, plus the real Baton Rouge Classic linking out), Club news (posts can be shared to LCA News), a Leaderboard from LCA results, and a relay Contact form with nearby clubs.
Club-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: Strava clubs (club page with events, posts and a weekly leaderboard; join/follow), Downriver ("Your first visit" questions), Grand Chess Tour standings (leaderboard), NC Chess Association (Last confirmed, Report outdated info, nearby clubs)
Club-B.dc.html.Trade-off: It only pays off if the club rep keeps posting; with sparse content the tabs look empty (Club-C is the fallback). The leaderboard needs a results archive matched by US Chess ID, and some players won't want to be ranked, hence the opt-out.
Club-B.dc.html.Build notes: Reuse club colour/logo (clubColors.ts, R2) and club news. Add `club_follows` (user or email, club_id) with a Resend digest from the daily-emails cron, `club_meetings` for next dates + ICS, and tournaments.club_id so club events use the existing registration/Stripe flow with "X of Y" counts. Add posts.club_id with a "share to LCA News" approval in PostsPanel, and members.home_club_id + leaderboard_opt_out. GET /api/clubs/:slug/leaderboard aggregates results by US Chess ID. POST /api/clubs/:id/message relays via Resend behind a Turnstile check. ClubDetailPage becomes an anchor-tabbed layout, and ManageClubPage gets colour, logo, description and first-visit fields.

Club-C.dc.html.What: A compact, honest profile for a club with little info (Gonzales Chess Club). A "2 of 7 details" meter puts "What we know" (missing facts stated plainly, each with an Add link) beside a "Help us complete this listing" form that takes a structured schedule (day, repeat rule, time, venue, cost, good-for, contact, "I run this club"). The map shows an approximate area instead of a fake pin. Below are nearby clubs with real next meetings, nearby tournaments and a "Claim this club" card.
Club-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: NC Chess Association (freshness loop: Last confirmed, report/complete info, nearby clubs; clubs maintain their own entries), Colorado "Add Club" (club submission form), parkrun (answer "when do you meet?" first)
Club-C.dc.html.Trade-off: The page asks visitors for data, and unverified suggestions need a volunteer to review them. Without that, the queue goes stale and the page stays empty. It's also less inviting than a full club page, by design.
Club-C.dc.html.Build notes: New `club_suggestions` table (club_id, fields JSON incl. structured meeting, submitter_email, status, reviewed_by) and POST /api/clubs/:id/suggest (Turnstile). AdminClubPage gets a Suggestions queue (approve → writes club_meetings/venue and stamps last_confirmed_at; "ask club" sends a Resend confirm email). A claim flow (POST /api/clubs/:id/claim → admin grants club_rep in roles.ts). ClubDetailPage picks the compact layout when the completeness score is under 4/7, shows an area circle when lat/lng are city-level only (ClubLocationPicker gains an "approximate" flag), and lists nearby clubs by distance with next_meeting from lcaTime.ts.

Start-Audit.dc.html.What: A factual audit of today's louisianachess.org: a 5-card "Fix first" strip (slideshow fails WCAG 2.2.2, 1.54:1 focus ring, 2.28:1 gold text, colour-only status dots, Register card below the player list on phones), then a table of 17 areas with KEEP strengths and FIX problems rated High/Med/Low, each tied to its file or component (59 keeps; 71 fixes: 14 High, 38 Med, 19 Low).
Start-Audit.dc.html.Borrowed from: codebase-inventory.md (page layouts, data model, the 52 UX issues), ux-evidence.md "Current site" findings and file map (WCAG 2.2, NN/g, web.dev), clubs-brands.md (what link-preview crawlers see).
Start-Audit.dc.html.Trade-off: severity is a reasoned rating from the research, not usage data; it is a snapshot of the code as read (the ticket-reply bug is marked "worth verifying"), and the board runs 1,600px taller than planned to fit 17 areas without clipping.

Sources.dc.html.What: One index of every source behind the board, 236 lines in four balanced columns: peer federations (27), tournament platforms (14), clubs and chess brands incl. Louisiana (34), cross-domain sites (53), evidence (62 lines covering NN/g, Baymard, GOV.UK, USWDS, WCAG 2.2, practitioners, platform docs and studies, each tagged with the UX-evidence section it informed), type and visual references by look (34), and the LCA codebase (12); each line gives the domain or path and what we took, with duplicates merged.
Sources.dc.html.Borrowed from: the reference and "Sites examined" sections of all seven research files.
Sources.dc.html.Trade-off: dense by design (a lookup page, not a read-through); links are plain text; related evidence articles share a line so ~120 references fit in 62 lines; the board is 1,350px taller than planned to avoid clipping.

Scan-C.dc.html.What: A printable notation kit that feeds the Scanner, as three Letter sheets: a scan-ready LCA scoresheet (four corner marks, one comb-ticked box per move, 50 moves on the front, fill-in result boxes, and when printed from the pairings a typed header plus a sheet-ID QR), a kids' notation cheat sheet (square names, piece letters, special marks, Morphy's Opera Game finish, a "your turn" drill that ends at the scanner), and two cut-out how-to-scan cards (TD-table card with QR; photo tips with good/retake diagrams). The bold part: a TD-printed sheet's QR files the scanned game under its pairing and offers the read result to the director.
Scan-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: Saint Louis Chess Club's free notation workbook and the clubs-brands "notation kit, Scanner, analysis" loop; notation as microcopy (clubs-brands); Chess67's posted venue QR codes and Lafayette Chess Club's QR-linked results; ChessRoster's Letter/A4 print reports; today's ScannerPage rules (log in, photos never stored, 20 scans a day, up to 3 pages).
Scan-C.dc.html.Trade-off: pre-printed sheets add a print step that needs final pairings, and reading marks, QR and result boxes is new backend work; players will still bring their own sheets, so the scanner must keep working without marks, and a read result stays a suggestion the TD confirms.
Scan-C.dc.html.Build notes: TournamentPrintPage gets a "Scoresheets" option (per round and section, pre-filled from the games table, plus a blank version) with Letter print CSS, four fixed corner marks and a client-side QR (e.g. the qrcode npm package) encoding /scanner?sheet=<signed token>; a new D1 migration adds `scoresheets` (token, tournament_id, round, section, board, game_id) and `game_scans` (game_id, member_id, pgn, result_read, scanned_at), functions/api/scan accepts the token (fills event and names, de-skews on the four marks, reads the result boxes) and saves the PGN to the game, tournaments/ResultsEntry shows "Scoresheet says 1-0 · Accept", and the cheat sheet and cards ship as a print route (/scanner/kit) or static PDFs.

Event-B.dc.html.What: Flagship hub for the 2027 Louisiana State Championship. It has a navy banner with a countdown and "23 of 160 registered", sticky tabs (Overview · Sections & prizes · Entries · Pairings · Standings · Hotel & travel · Past champions) and a live-strip slot that appears only Sep 4–6. The 3-day and 2-day schedules sit side by side and merge at Round 4. Side events (Labor Day Scholastic, State Blitz, LCA annual business meeting) are added in the same checkout. It also has round alerts, a hotel block card, past champions from the honor roll and a per-event link preview.
Event-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: Grand Chess Tour / FIDE Candidates (event tabs as a mini-microsite), Tata Steel Chess (countdown), London Chess Classic (side events grouped with the main event), Marshall / Norway Chess (live mode), KingRegistration (parallel schedules; Register · Entries · Pairings · Standings under the title), Chess67 / ChessRoster / Luma (registration card + phone sticky bar), AskFRED (add to calendar).
Event-B.dc.html.Trade-off: A lot of page for one weekend a year. Pairings and Standings sit empty for 11 months, and volunteers must feed in the hotel, meeting room and agenda details or the hub looks half-built.
Event-B.dc.html.Build notes: D1: tournaments.is_flagship, side events via parent_tournament_id, schedule_tracks (track, round, starts_at, time_control), and registration line items so side events and meeting RSVPs share one Stripe Checkout. TournamentDetailPage becomes a tabbed hub reusing StandingsTable/Crosstable/PrizeWinners and champions.ts data. The live strip is driven by lcaTime.ts plus the pairings API. Round alerts use Resend plus Web Push (new push_subscriptions table, functions/api/tournaments/[id]/follow). The link preview is an OG image from a Pages Function (satori + resvg-wasm) at /og/tournaments/[slug].png. Page grew from 2600 to 3000 tall.

Event-C.dc.html.What: The same 2027 Paul Morphy Open page at three moments, side by side. Before (Tue, Jun 1): price today, how full each section is, who's coming, and Register in the phone bar. During (Sat, Jun 12, 7:40 PM, live Round 3): a "Your board" card, pairings by section, TD notes, round alerts and a site-wide live banner. After (Mon, Jun 14): winners, recap, photos, crosstable, scanner games and the next LCA event. Entries closing, the first pairing and the last result switch the page automatically.
Event-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: Marshall / Columbia / Norway Chess (live mode via the site banner), start.gg and Chesstide (round and check-in banners), Luma / Meetup / Dice (button states that follow event status), Grand Chess Tour / FIDE Candidates (photos and past-edition tabs), KingRegistration (Register · Entries · Pairings · Standings under the title).
Event-C.dc.html.Trade-off: The automatic switch is only as good as the data. A late result entry or a section that finishes hours after the others leaves the page in the wrong mode, so TDs need an override and the edge cases need testing.
Event-C.dc.html.Build notes: New lib/eventPhase.ts derives before/live/final from tournaments + rounds + results (entry close, first pairing published_at, all results in). TournamentDetailPage and AnnouncementBanner use it for the automatic "Live" banner. New td_notes table + POST functions/api/tournaments/[id]/notes from TournamentManagePage, fanned out to followers via Resend/Web Push. "Your board" comes from the pairings API matched to the viewer's registration. The recap is a news-post draft seeded from PrizeWinners/standings (PostsPanel), the photo album lives in R2, and games link to scanner PGNs.

Event-E.dc.html.What: Internal LCA page for a real clearinghouse listing: Mississippi State Championship, Sat–Sun, Oct 17–18, Canton, MS, Mississippi Chess Association. It has one gold "Register on organizer site" exit and a facts card with the same fields in the same order on every partner event, which says plainly what the feed lacks (fees, sections, round times). A source line shows the daily sync. Visitors can watch the listing (with its change history) and see a regional map with drive times from Louisiana cities. Below that: "Also near Canton" (real feed events in Jackson, Ridgeland and Scott County), the Louisiana events the weekends before and after (Lafayette Open, Baton Rouge Classic), "Report a problem", an auto-linked US Chess crosstable after the event, and a link preview.
Event-E.dc.html.Borrowed from: NC Chess Association (internal pages for clearinghouse events, consistent facts card, "Register on organizer site ↗", "Also in [city]"), AskFRED (add to calendar), Meetup / Luma (event page with the map in the side column).
Event-E.dc.html.Trade-off: Partner pages are thin by nature (no fees or status in the feed), and the drive times and change alerts depend on geocoding and a reliable daily diff. Every Register click still sends the visitor away.
Event-E.dc.html.Build notes: The Gulf South clearinghouse sync Worker stores listing snapshots (new clearinghouse_listing_versions table), diffs them daily and emails rows in a new listing_watchers table via Resend. Geocode each city/venue once (Google Geocoding) to lat/lng, for "Also near" (haversine ≤60 mi) and for Distance Matrix drive times cached per Louisiana hub city. Add a partner variant of TournamentDetailPage with LCAMap. "Report a problem" posts to functions/api/support with listing_id attached. After the end date, a best-effort US Chess crosstable link comes from an event lookup in functions/api/uscf. Page is 2250 tall, not 2000.

Reg-C.dc.html.What: A one-page household checkout for the Paul Morphy Open & Morphy Scholastic. Danielle Robichaux ticks saved players (herself, Maya, Leo; no child logins). Each player gets a panel showing only the sections they can enter by rating, one yes/no grade box for grade-capped sections ("Maya is in 8th grade or below"), per-round bye boxes, and their US Chess membership state: current, or expired with a weekly re-check. Optional LCA membership compares Family $25 with separate memberships, with an honest net cost. A sticky "Check and pay" summary has Change links and a live total including card processing ($87.77). One Stripe payment produces one confirmation and Withdraw link per player. Spots are held during checkout, and if a section fills only that player goes to the waitlist.
Reg-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: ChessRoster (one section panel per player, one fee table, one payment), AskFRED / Chess67 / onlineregistration.cc ("Who's playing?" household picker), ACTIVE (per-person type, one payment, 15-minute hold timer), HMRC / MOJ (add-to-a-list), GOV.UK (check your answers with Change links; what happens next), Baymard (total shown upfront, trust cues), Eventbrite (per-attendee model, avoiding Meetup's guest trap), RunSignup (waitlist claim windows), KingRegistration (US Chess ID lookup, expiry flags).
Reg-C.dc.html.Trade-off: A long page for a single adult entering one section, and the edge cases multiply: playing up, one child's section filling mid-checkout, partial refunds on one payment. Passing on the processing fee is a board policy call.
Reg-C.dc.html.Build notes: Saved players come from family.ts / FamilyRegistrationPanel. New registration_orders table (one Stripe Checkout Session, line items per player plus membership), registrations.order_id, and per-player Stripe partial refunds on withdraw. Eligibility comes from sectionRules.ts plus a per-section grade-cap confirm (extend GradeConfirm). pricing.ts prices each line (early/member). New section_holds table with 15-minute expiry swept by a cron. US Chess status via UscfSearchInput / functions/api/uscf, plus a weekly Worker cron that re-checks expiry and emails via Resend. Confirmations per player via Resend. Page is 2700 tall, not 2400.

Reg-D.dc.html.What: Guest-first quick entry for the Paul Morphy Open, on desktop and two phones. Typing a US Chess ID fills in name, rating and membership expiry ("Found: Sam Nguyen · 1650 · member through Nov 30, 2027"), with search by name as a fallback. Then email, a section from the eligible ones only, and optional byes: four fields here plus four card fields on Stripe, or none with Apple Pay / Google Pay. A summary with Change links shows the full total before the same-tab Stripe redirect. The receipt link lets guests switch section or withdraw without an account. Back from Stripe, "Save these details — create an account" is offered as a passwordless email link. The phone version opens from a QR code on the event flyer.
Reg-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: KingRegistration and ECF (US Chess ID or last-name lookup fills name, rating, expiry), Luma (guest-first, account after payment), Baymard (8 fields instead of 11.3; prominent guest path; total upfront; visible security), NN/g (login walls), GOV.UK (eligibility first, check your answers, what happens next), Stripe Checkout (same-tab redirect), WCAG 3.3.8 (email-link sign-in).
Reg-D.dc.html.Trade-off: Guest entries scatter player data outside accounts (duplicates, a typo'd email locks someone out of their manage link). It also depends on a reliable US Chess lookup, and players without an ID still need a slower path.
Reg-D.dc.html.Build notes: New public route /tournaments/:slug/enter (RegisterPage guest mode) using UscfSearchInput / functions/api/uscf for lookup and expiry, sectionRules.ts for eligible sections and pricing.ts for the early/member price (member status matched by US Chess ID). Registrations allow guest_email with a signed manage_token (HMAC) emailed via Resend for change/withdraw. Stripe Checkout uses customer_email and success_url back to /enter/done. After payment, a Supabase Auth magic link (signInWithOtp) creates the account and claims guest registrations by email + US Chess ID. Flyer QR codes come from TournamentPrintPage.

About-A.dc.html.What: Transparency hub for About: who LCA is (real stats), a next-board-meeting card (Tue, Nov 10 · agenda · add to calendar), bylaws as a web page with per-article "Changed" flags, a records list where every item carries a status and last-updated date, a plain-language minutes recap tagged Notable/Routine, "write to a seat, not a person" contacts, a year-at-a-glance money table with [Amount] placeholders, and elections as four dated steps.
About-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Chicago Councilmatic (next-meeting card + plain-language recap), NN/g and data.gov (minutes and bylaws as web pages with "Last updated"), North Carolina Chess Association (minutes/treasury by year with "Last updated"), United Way Lee (records by type, newest first), Keep a Changelog (bylaw change log), charity: water / ProPublica and Minnesota (financials by year), Southern California (election results with vote counts).
About-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Only builds trust if the Secretary and Treasurer keep it current; stale stamps or empty [Amount] cells would advertise neglect, and every meeting needs a plain-language recap.
About-A.dc.html.Build notes: New board_meetings table (date, time, mode, agenda, recap items tagged notable/routine) and status/last_updated on governance docs; bylaws as HTML articles with a change log (GovernanceDocuments, RichTextEditor); seat-addressed messages routed into BoardInboxPage via the seats in BoardSeatsPanel; finance summary rows entered from the approved treasurer's report; election steps as dated fields; AboutPage becomes a hub with a section sub-nav.

Club-A.dc.html.What: Visit-first Downriver Chess Club page: "Tonight, 7:00 PM · Mon, Oct 5" as the headline, Turtle Bay (1119 Decatur St) with a mini map and honest access notes (two flights of stairs, a bar, parking placeholder), cost and G/15 in plain words, a four-step "Your first visit" story with a before-you-go card, Downriver's clearinghouse tournaments, club news and photo slots (Sample), next club nights with skipped dates (Thu, Nov 26 Thanksgiving), "Schedule confirmed" stamp, "Report outdated info", other New Orleans clubs.
Club-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Downriver Chess (its "Your first visit!" story, honest Turtle Bay notes, no club night on Saints games), parkrun (meeting time as headline, first-visit box), North Carolina Chess Association (club page order, "Listing last updated"), Luma and Strava (follow + reminder the day before), England Football / USA Swimming (affiliation badge).
Club-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Downriver is the richest case; most of the 25 clubs can't supply venue notes, first-visit copy or photos, so their pages would be mostly brackets unless paired with a compact fallback (Club-C).
Club-A.dc.html.Build notes: Structured club schedules (weekday, time, recurrence such as 1st/3rd, per-day venue) plus a skipped-dates table to compute "next club night"; new club fields for access/age policy/parking/first-visit text and confirmed_at; club_follows table + day-before reminder in the Resend daily-emails cron; per-club .ics (Pages Function); club tournaments matched from the clearinghouse by organizer; club_news and R2 photos; ClubDetailPage reworked, ManageClubPage gains the fields.

Clubs-D.dc.html.What: Directory of all 25 real clubs as A–Z cards (logo slot or initials, club-colour dot, meeting day/time and venue, time control in plain words, up to three tags, "Confirmed" month) with search, a region mini-map and region list with counts, quick chips with live counts (Meets today 6, Weekends, Kids welcome, Rated, Free, Lessons), A–Z / Meets soonest / Nearest sort, an A–Z jump bar, honest "Schedule not listed · Tell us" on the 7 clubs without schedules, and a rep freshness loop ("Still accurate").

Clubs-D.dc.html.Trade-off: 25 cards make a long scroll and shrink geography to a mini-map; most cards will show initials rather than logos; an A–Z bar is heavy for 25 clubs.
Clubs-D.dc.html.Build notes: Structured meeting schedules for "Meets today"/"Meets soonest" (Central time via lcaTime.ts); tags and region on clubs (regions.ts — live region data is blank); confirmed_at set by a "Still accurate" action in ManageClubPage/Workspace; "Report outdated info" opens a support ticket; filters and sort in the URL; logos from R2, colours from clubColors.ts; ClubsPage card grid with a Cards/Map toggle to LCAMap.

Event-A.dc.html.What: 2027 Paul Morphy Open (Sample details) with fact tiles that translate chess shorthand, a sticky registration card (38 of 60, section picker, early/regular/late ladder with dates, member price, Register / Register my family, plus the button's other states: opens-remind, waitlist, registered, live, final), section cards with how full and prizes, round-time agenda with add-to-calendar, a $1,500 prize table, "Who's coming" sorted by rating with section counts and an update stamp, venue placeholders with nearby clubs, a "Good to know" rules strip, and a share block showing the link-preview card.
Event-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Luma (sticky two-column card, button states, "38 registered — names and 36 others"), Chess67 / ChessRoster (registration card; utility row Contact TD · Add to calendar · Share · QR), Eventbrite ("Good to know" strip, round times as agenda), KingRegistration / Welsh entrants / Chess-Results (entries by rating with section counts, "Updated … · ratings" stamp), AskFRED (one eligibility sentence per section), KingRegistration's LCA codes (FAMILY / LUNCH), Chess67's "Loading…" previews as the anti-pattern behind per-event link previews.
Event-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Very long page that needs a lot of TD-entered data per event (caps, price dates, venue notes); a public rating-sorted entry list puts kids' names and ratings on the page (normal at rated events, but parents notice).
Event-A.dc.html.Build notes: TournamentDetailPage gets the sticky card driven by pricing.ts (early/regular/late + member), per-section caps and counts, waitlist and RegistrationReminderButton states; entries API sorted by rating with club join and rating-supplement month; per-round .ics (Pages Function); server-rendered og: tags + generated image for /tournaments/:slug (Pages Function); FamilyRegistrationPanel behind "Register my family"; discount codes in pricing.ts.

Event-D.dc.html.What: Festival microsite for the Paul Morphy Open + Morphy Scholastic + Friday Night Blitz (Sample, Fri–Sun, Jun 11–13, 2027): sticky festival bar, photo hero with countdown and "112 players registered across 3 events", all three events with sections, eligibility as one yes/no box, fees and "X of Y", an Open + Blitz bundle, side events (simul, Morphy talk), an hour-by-hour schedule filterable by event with "add just my rounds", a Morphy heritage block with the Opera Game final position, a visit block (venue, hotel rate, drive times, food), FAQ, sponsor slots and a Facebook preview.
Event-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: London Chess Classic and the Ken Ferguson Memorial (festival grouping with side events), Grand Chess Tour / FIDE Candidates (event pages as mini-microsites), Tata Steel Chess and Saint Louis Chess Club (visit and heritage blocks), ChessRoster (bundle with "You save"), Historic New Orleans Collection and 64 Parishes (Morphy links).
Event-D.dc.html.Trade-off: Pays off for one or two flagship weekends a year and needs a volunteer for hotel, sponsor, speaker and venue content; a second event template to maintain.
Event-D.dc.html.Build notes: New festivals (event group) table linking several tournaments with shared venue/hotel/sponsor fields; bundle pricing in pricing.ts and multi-line Stripe Checkout; schedule items (incl. side events) with per-player .ics; festival-level counts; FamilyRegistrationPanel + GradeConfirm for the scholastic; per-festival og: preview via Pages Function; static FEN board for the Opera Game; LCAMap for the venue map.

Home-A.dc.html.What: The next registerable event (Lafayette Open 2026) as the hero card — weekday dates, check-in and round 1, time control in plain words, sections, 38 of 60 with spots left and the next price deadline, Register from $30 — with an inset of the same slot in "Live · Round 3 pairings posted" mode; then three start-here tasks, a dated upcoming list (LCA vs Partner status, "Add Gulf South", .ics), "This week at the clubs" (tonight + later this week, 19 meetings), latest State Championship results (Sample), the four real membership tiers, news and the Facebook rail.
Home-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Mississippi Scholastic Chess Association ("Next Event" block) and Tata Steel (countdown), Luma / USA Ultimate (mission line + next real event with "X of Y"), Saint Louis Chess Club "OPEN TODAY" and Melbourne's weekday list (this-week strip), lichess / Chess-Results / Chess67 (live first), England / Norway federations (calendar subscribe).
Home-A.dc.html.Trade-off: The hero only shines when the next event registers on LCA; when it's a partner listing it loses the count and Register, and the page is long and dense below the fold.
Home-A.dc.html.Build notes: HomePage hero query = next tournament with registration open (count, cap, next price step from pricing.ts), swapping to live mode once the current round's pairings are published; structured club schedules for "This week" (lcaTime.ts); clearinghouse toggle; site-wide .ics feed (Pages Function); StandingsTable for latest results; FacebookFeed rail unchanged.

Home-B.dc.html.What: Search-first homepage: one box for tournaments, clubs and players with grouped type-ahead (shown mid-search for "baton"), quick picks (This weekend · Scholastic · Near me · Rated · Free), stats that are links (25+ clubs, 7 regions, 11 tournaments, 300+ members), a next-up line, then compact panels: next 5 tournaments, clubs near you (last region or location), latest results, player lookup, "Am I an LCA member?", news, scholastic events, board items, popular pages, and a one-line membership band.
Home-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: North Carolina Chess Association (search-first hero with clickable stats), Chess67 / ChessRoster time chips and Seattle Chess Club tags (quick picks), US Rowing (warm club finder), KingRegistration / ECF (lookup by ID or name).
Home-B.dc.html.Trade-off: Search is only as good as its index and the US Chess lookup; a search box shows less life than an event hero, and many small panels compete for attention.
Home-B.dc.html.Build notes: New /api/search over tournaments, clubs and posts, with players through the existing uscf lookup (UscfSearchInput); quick picks as URL filters on TournamentsPage/ClubsPage; geolocation only on "Use my location", last region remembered locally; status-only membership check endpoint (membership API, no contact details); popular pages static.

Home-D.dc.html.What: Newspaper front page: dateline + "Updated" time, a bulletin line (Lafayette Open as a partner event; turns live on LCA event days), a lead State Championship recap (Sample) with section winners, a results box with the tiebreak explained and an upset of the weekend, a coming-up rail incl. the 2027 TOC Qualifier, secondary stories, a reigning-champions band, a Morphy heritage feature with timeline, links and an Opera Game mate-in-two, an "Around the state" stream of club and Facebook posts, and four closing modules (join, next board meeting, organizers, donate).
Home-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: Substack (Newspaper/Feature hero modes), Central Florida (recap with winners box), World Chess Hall of Fame (champion cards), Tata Steel (heritage block) with Historic New Orleans Collection and 64 Parishes links, The Verge Storystream (mixed short-post stream).
Home-D.dc.html.Trade-off: Needs steady editorial output (recaps, photos, short posts); without a volunteer writer the dateline makes staleness obvious within weeks.
Home-D.dc.html.Build notes: posts gain a lead flag, hero photo (R2), byline and read time; results box from StandingsTable/Crosstable data of the latest final event; champions band from champions.ts / ChampionsPanel; puzzle as a static FEN board component; "Around the state" merges club_news with the server-side FacebookFeed; bulletin line reads tournament round status.

Home-E.dc.html.What: Three photo doors ("I want to play" / "My child plays" / "I run a club or tournament"), three links each landing on shared, pre-filtered pages (landing named in grey), an escape row for people who fit none or several, next events grouped open / scholastic / LCA championships (Sample 2027 LCA dates, "18 of 80"), a clubs map teaser with region counts and tonight's meetings, and the membership tiers.
Home-E.dc.html.Borrowed from: Charlotte Chess Center (three-door branching, without its lead form), Ireland's federation (audience row) tempered by NN/g's audience-navigation warning (doors are shortcuts; the main menu stays task-based), Harvard design system (short grouped teasers ending in "All …"), US Rowing (warm finder with region buttons).
Home-E.dc.html.Trade-off: Doors make visitors pick an identity and add a click; a playing parent fits two doors, and the grouped lists repeat events.
Home-E.dc.html.Build notes: Doors are static links with URL filter presets (TournamentsPage, ClubsPage, Workspace); grouped teasers from tournaments + clearinghouse by eligibility and LCA-run flag; LCAMap teaser with region counts and "meets tonight" pins from structured club schedules; live strip from round status.

Live-D.dc.html.What: Hall TV screen for the 2027 Paul Morphy Open (Sample): Round 3 U1800 pairings in two big columns (colour, name, rating, points going in), round start with countdown and posted time, byes spelled out, a QR to the phone view ("Your board, on your phone"), a round timeline, and a cycling queue (Open / U1800 / U1400 / U1000 pairings, then standings once results arrive) with TD keys.
Live-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: ChessRoster (/live TV mode cycling pairings and standings), Chesstide / Chess-Results / Chess67's Campbell story (hall QR to the live page), Chesstide (byes in words), IRLchess / SwissSys (scores going in).
Live-D.dc.html.Trade-off: Only for LCA-run events paired on the site, and needs a screen plus laptop at the venue; 15-second paging means a player may wait up to a minute for their section.
Live-D.dc.html.Build notes: New /tournaments/:id/live route beside TournamentPairingsPage that polls the pairings/standings API, cycles sections on a timer with keyboard pause/step, and draws a QR (client-side QR library) to a short link; round times from the tournament; no new tables.

Looks-3-Minimal-Tile.dc.html.What: Style tile for "Modern Tech-Minimal — the club, engineered": idea / best for / watch out, Geist + Geist Mono + one Instrument Serif accent, light and dark palettes with contrast ratios (gold as fill only on white, #866a1e for gold text), components (navy glass header with ⌘K search, buttons, all status tags, US Chess ID input, chips, event card and row), chess data (pairings row, crosstable cells, rating deltas, standings with modified median + Solkoff, round timeline, Opera Game board), dot-grid / clock-bar motif, navy-to-gold duotone, Lucide icon style, Dos and Don'ts.

Looks-3-Minimal-Tile.dc.html.Build notes: Tailwind/shadcn token pass (6/12 radii, hairline borders, Geist Mono tabular data), a real dark theme starting from #0b1220, Instrument Serif via Google Fonts for one accent, Lucide at 1.5px, a ⌘K palette (shadcn Command / cmdk) over a search endpoint, duotone photo CSS.

Nav-IA.dc.html.What: The ~40 pages filed three ways side by side — (1) Task and topic (recommended; About as a click dropdown), (2) Audience hubs with "in 2/3 hubs" duplication badges, (3) Lean four + More — each with pros/cons, a "Today" column describing the live Navbar/Footer and its four issues, and a table of where Scanner, Champions, Governance docs, Donate, My LCA and Workspace land. News-A.dc.html.What: News as one featured results story (State Championship, Sample) with section winners, pinned items that expire on a set date, month-grouped dated rows with category chips and counts, a "From our Facebook page" rail fed server-side, a "Post club news" prompt for reps, "Load 10 more" and a yearly archive.
News-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Substack (Feature hero mode), Chess Scotland (pinned news), NN/g (rows not cards, "Load more" instead of infinite scroll), Central Florida (recap teaser with winners), the current site's server-side Facebook feed (kept per ux-evidence's Fashion ID note).

News-A.dc.html.Build notes: posts gain category, featured flag and pinned_until (PostsPanel); club_news posted from Workspace with the club colour; category filter in the URL; paginated list API; FacebookFeed rail unchanged; "Email updates" via a Resend list.

News-B.dc.html.Build notes: New /api/news/stream merging posts, club_news, final results, FacebookFeed items and banners into one typed, date-sorted list with per-type counts; NewsPage rebuilt as a stream with type/club filters in the URL; colours from clubColors.ts.

Reg-A.dc.html.What: Registration stays inside the event page's sticky card: five states beside a dimmed 2027 Paul Morphy Open page — at rest with prices and 38 of 60; "Who's playing?" (Danielle, Maya, Leo, someone else); section + one-box eligibility + byes by round with day and time, ineligible sections greyed with the reason; check your answers with an itemized total; paid, then what happens next (check-in, pairings by email, calendar, receipts).
Reg-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Chess67 / ChessRoster / Luma (registration card in the right column), AskFRED / Chess67 / onlineregistration.cc ("Who's playing?" household picker), ChessRoster / AskFRED (eligibility with reason, running itemized total), GOV.UK (check your answers), ChessRoster / Luma / start.gg (a confirmation that does something).
Reg-A.dc.html.Trade-off: A narrow card gets cramped for families with per-player sections and byes, and on phones it becomes a full-height sheet anyway.
Reg-A.dc.html.Build notes: Card state machine in TournamentDetailPage using FamilyRegistrationPanel / family.ts, GradeConfirm for the yes/no box, sectionRules.ts eligibility with reasons, per-round bye requests, pricing.ts totals; Stripe Checkout redirect back to the card (stripe API), receipts via Resend, .ics.

Reg-B.dc.html.What: Five phones, one question per screen for Jordan Lee (Sample): who's playing, then which section (only eligible ones, priced with early + member discounts, "Which section fits me?"), then byes by round plus an inline US Chess ID check whose expiry warning never blocks, then check your answers with Change links and the full total, then a confirmation that leads with the renew-US-Chess to-do.
Reg-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: GOV.UK (one question per page, check your answers), ChessRoster (step-by-step Player → Section → Byes → Pay), KingRegistration / ECF (ID lookup fills name, rating, expiry), Chess67 (warn, don't block, on lapsed membership).
Reg-B.dc.html.Trade-off: More taps than a one-card form for regulars who already know their section, and a separate flow from the event page.
Reg-B.dc.html.Build notes: RegisterPage as a 4-step wizard + confirmation that keeps answers on Back; UscfSearchInput / UsChessMembership inline with expiry checked against the event date; reminder email before expiry via the daily-emails Worker; pricing.ts member + early discounts; Stripe Checkout in the same tab.

Schol-A.dc.html.What: Parent guide to a first scholastic tournament: quick facts, a numbered jump bar, a check-in-to-awards timeline (Sample times, "~" for rounds that start when the last ends), a what-to-bring checklist, chess words in plain English, grade-band sections, costs (real $5 / $25 memberships, Sample entries, lunch and sibling discounts), safety, "What LCA keeps about your child", FAQ, the real upcoming scholastic events (NOLA Youth Chess meets, Ken Ferguson Scholastic, SWLA Regional) plus a Sample State Scholastic, email signup and a share card.
Schol-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: New South Wales / Virginia / Ireland / England federations ("Your first tournament" path), AskFRED (first-tournament guide with glossary and checklist), LCA's own KingRegistration copy (timeline, 30-minute forfeit rule, lunch/sibling codes), Saint Louis Chess Club footer and ChessKid's list (safety block, what's collected), England Football (parent page order).
Schol-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Very long and content-heavy; times and fees must stay in sync with real events, and the lunch discount implies asking families something the privacy card doesn't list.
Schol-A.dc.html.Build notes: Mostly content in ScholasticPage plus a glossary tooltip component and a checklist saved locally; scholastic events from tournaments + clearinghouse filtered by eligibility; GradeConfirm for the eligibility box; Resend audience for the monthly email; per-page og: preview.

Tourn-A.dc.html.What: Month-grouped agenda (16 events Oct–Dec, LCA and Gulf South partner) with date blocks, status in words, "X of Y registered" with fill bars and deadlines on LCA rows, lighter partner rows that say where entry happens, one row of filter chips (When · Type · Region · Rated · LCA-run / Partner) with removable applied chips, live count, Clear all and "Copy link to this view", a filter-following .ics / Google Calendar feed, a new-to-tournaments glossary, latest results and "Submit an event".
Tourn-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: the federations research's top idea (one chip row incl. LCA-run vs clearinghouse), Chess67 / ChessRoster (time chips + LCA-run toggle), Tabroom / Luma (status in words), ChessRoster / NAChessHub (grouped by month with load more), NN/g and Baymard (removable chips, count, filters in the URL), England and Norway (calendar subscribe), Resident Advisor (count-headed date list).
Tourn-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Partner rows (12 of 16) are thin by necessity and dominate the list; Calendar and Map are only tabs here.
Tourn-A.dc.html.Build notes: TournamentsPage filters serialized to the URL; tournaments + clearinghouse merged with a source flag and per-month counts; RegistrationReminderButton for "Notify me"; .ics / Google feed as a Pages Function honouring the same filter params; sticky month headers; "Submit an event" into an admin/support queue.

Live-A.dc.html.What: Three phones across one Saturday evening (all Sample data, matching Live-D's Round 3). (1) The round-ready banner, then find-your-board by typing a few letters, with a follow star on each match. (2) A pinned "Board 7 · You have White · vs Sam Nguyen 1650 · starts 7:00 PM" card in big type, with a text-size toggle, "Updated 2 min ago", the player's rounds so far, and result reporting after the game. (3) A parent's "My players" strip for Maya and Leo (board, colour, opponent, result and score), with live U1400 standings and email alerts. A round-ready email preview sits above the phones.
Live-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Chess67 (round-posted message "You are playing White against … on board 4"), start.gg / melee.gg (pinned "your board" card), Tabroom and Meet Mobile (follow lists, one-click stop-all alerts), ChessRoster (results by link or reply, provisional until the director confirms), Chesstide / Chess-Results (type-to-filter names).
Live-A.dc.html.Trade-off: Results reported by players need the opponent's confirmation plus a TD review queue, or disputes move from the TD table to the website. Alerts only help if the TD publishes pairings on the site the moment they're made.
Live-A.dc.html.Build notes: New D1 tables `follows` (device token or user → registration), `round_alerts` (email, verified, unsubscribed_at) and `result_reports` (pairing, reporter, result, status). Pages Functions `api/tournaments/[id]/live` (polled every 60 s with ETag, or SSE), `api/follows` and `api/results/report`. Resend sends the email when the TD publishes a round (via a queue or the daily-emails Worker); web push comes later. New components `FindPlayer`, `LiveBoardCard`, `FollowStrip` and `TextSizeToggle`; `TournamentPairingsPage` and `ResultsEntry` (TD confirm queue) are extended. Note: Round 3 starts at 7:00 PM to match the published Live-D schedule (the brief said 2:30 PM).

Live-B.dc.html.What: The main live pairings page, shown at 8:41 PM Saturday with Round 3 in progress and 5 of 13 U1800 results in. It has round tabs and section chips with counts, type-to-find (it highlights the matching row), by-board or A–Z order, a text-size toggle remembered on the device, and "Updated 1 min ago" with refresh every 60 s. A pinned "Your game" card carries a Report result button. The pairings are a real table (Bd · White · Rtg · Pts · Result · Black · Rtg · Pts) with a frozen board column; results arrive live, byes are labelled, and the other sections collapse to a progress line. The sidebar holds the round schedule, email round alerts, the venue QR with hall-TV and print links, and a legend, followed by a three-step "First tournament?" card.
Live-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: IRLchess / SwissSys (board rows with scores, "Bd · White (2½) · result · Black"), SwissSys (by-board and alphabetical orders), Chess-Results / Chesstide (type to filter), Chess67 and start.gg (pinned your-board card), and from ux-evidence, NN/g and USWDS (caption, scope, a labelled scroll region you can reach by keyboard, frozen first column).
Live-B.dc.html.Trade-off: One page for every section means long scrolling at big events. Collapsing the other sections keeps it short but hides boards that spectators may expect to see.
Live-B.dc.html.Build notes: Extend `TournamentPairingsPage` with `round`, `section` and `q` URL params and a new `PairingsTable` (caption, `scope`, sticky board column, rating/points columns marked `k-hide-sm` so phones show Bd · White · Result · Black). Poll `GET api/tournaments/[id]/live?round=N` every 60 s with ETag / If-None-Match; it returns pairings, results, byes and per-section progress. `TextSizeToggle` uses localStorage. Reuse `LiveBoardCard`, `round_alerts` and Resend from Live-A. QR codes come from an SVG QR library (e.g. the `qrcode` npm package).

Live-C.dc.html.What: Final U1800 results (Sample data, internally consistent with Live-D's Round 3). One place-ordered "standings + crosstable" table in SwissSys style. Round cells read like "W ○ 17": letter, tint and a hollow (White) or filled (Black) dot, so colour is never the only signal. Scores use ½. Place and Player stay frozen when you scroll sideways. Tiebreak columns carry full names, with a hover explanation that works an example. A column chooser covers Rounds, Tiebreaks and Prizes, plus a text-size toggle. Above the table: a prize-winners panel that applies the US Chess tie-split and one-cash-prize rules in plain words (2nd–4th share $200; Best U1600 passes to Jacob because Devin's share is larger), a found-player card (place, prize, unofficial rating estimate, round-by-round list that doubles as the phone view) and a "How ties are broken" legend. A TD-only close-out panel has pre-upload checks and "Download US Chess report".
Live-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: ChessRoster / SwissSys (standings with W17 / L2 / D3 / H / B / U cells and a prize column; on phones, tables become cards with a round-by-round strip), Chess-Results ("Search for player", ranking crosstable), AskFRED / Chess-Results (results headline "N players · 5 rounds · avg"), Chess67 (checks before the rating report), ux-evidence (frozen Place and Player, tiebreaks spelled out, caption and scope).
Live-C.dc.html.Trade-off: The combined table is wide (14 columns) and dense. On phones it leans on the column chooser and the player card, and opponent pairing numbers need tap-to-jump to feel friendly.
Live-C.dc.html.Build notes: Merge `StandingsTable` and `Crosstable` into one `ResultsGrid` with two sticky columns, a `ResultCell` (letter, tint, dot, ½), header tooltips, and the column choice saved in localStorage. The standings API already returns modifiedMedian, solkoff, cumulative, oppCumulative and blacks. New `lib/prizes.ts` pools and splits tied place prizes and applies the one-cash-prize rule to `PrizesEditor` data, shown through `PrizeWinners`. New `lib/ratingEstimate.ts` (US Chess formula, labelled unofficial). New player-page route `/players/:uscfId` for the results archive and rating history. The US Chess report reuses `uschessUpload.ts` and `UsChessUploadPanel`, with added pre-flight checks.

Live-E.dc.html.What: Six letter-size sheets (560×725) on a neutral ground, each captioned, all built from the same live data (Sample, consistent with Live-B/C/D). (1) Hall poster with a QR placeholder drawn as an SVG grid, the short link louisianachess.org/morphy27, the round times and "Phones off and away once clocks start". (2) U1800 Round 3 pairings A–Z, with byes giving their reason. (3) Pairings by board with ratings, points and circle-the-result columns. (4) Standings after Round 2 with tiebreaks named in full. (5) Final wall chart in pairing-number order, where hollow and filled dots (shape, not colour) mark White and Black. (6) A one-page final report for the board and treasurer, with bracketed blanks for unknowns. A bottom band covers when to print what, the print rules built in, and optional board cards carrying a per-board QR for result reporting.
Live-E.dc.html.Borrowed from: Chess67 Campbell story (two posted QR codes ended "the frantic scramble to print"), Chesstide / Chess-Results / Chess67 (hall poster with QR), Chesstide / SwissSys (alphabetical sheet with bye reasons, wall chart, one-page final report), ChessRoster (every report as a branded PDF in Letter), ux-evidence (print CSS, `break-inside: avoid`, nothing that depends on colour).
Live-E.dc.html.Trade-off: Paper never fully goes away at a volunteer event, and two sources of truth (sheet and site) can drift unless results circled on paper are entered right away. The per-board QR cards add a setup step for whoever lays out the tables.
Live-E.dc.html.Build notes: Extend `TournamentPrintPage` with `poster`, `alpha`, `board`, `standings`, `wallchart` and `final-report` views. Use `@media print` with Letter at 100%, `break-inside: avoid` on rows, one section per page and black-and-white-safe glyphs. Add a "Print round N set" action that opens one combined print view. Generate QR codes as SVG client-side (e.g. the `qrcode` npm package) from a new `short_slug` column on tournaments, served by a Pages Function redirect `/[slug]` → the live page. Per-board QR cards deep-link to `api/results/report?pairing=…`. The final report pulls Stripe entry totals from the registrations API and the prize split from `lib/prizes.ts` (Live-C), and can be emailed to the board as a PDF through Resend. Shared sample data (live group): the U1800 tournament for Live-A/B/C/E comes from notes/live_u1800_data.py and notes/live_u1800_final.py. Rounds 1–2 were rebuilt so Live-D's published Round 3 (pairings, colours, points) follows exactly; Rounds 4–5 were Swiss-paired. Every result mirrors, no one has three of a colour in a row, and the US Chess tiebreaks were computed (unplayed games count ½ in an opponent's score and 0 in the player's own). Story: Devin Batiste (Bd 7, White vs Sam Nguyen in Round 3) finishes tied 2nd–4th; Isaac Dupre wins on 4½.

Looks-1-Heritage-Tile.dc.html.What: Style tile for "Heritage Club — since 1915": Libre Caslon Display headlines, Source Serif 4 text with true small caps and tabular figures, IBM Plex Mono for notation; cream paper, navy ink, gold only for rules/seals/text on navy; a round seal built from the rook-shaped mark; printed-program tables (W/D/L letters + baize wins + piece-color squares, real ½, small-caps "p" for provisional); the Opera Game final position; navy–cream duotone photo with fine grain in a cream mat; 1.25px Lucide icons.
Looks-1-Heritage-Tile.dc.html.Borrowed from: Pentagram's World Chess identity ("a study, not a stage": wood, brass, paper), Marshall Chess Club (heritage from copy and type, not costume), World Chess Hall of Fame (restraint), The Masters (leaderboard-first, honor-board standings), Tata Steel Chess (section cards); table rules from Chess-Results, Butterick and Ström via the data-typography research.
Looks-1-Heritage-Tile.dc.html.Trade-off: Weakest at fast-changing live data, and serif small caps get fussy in dense admin/workspace UI; brand gold can never be text on cream (2.05:1), so it recedes to rules and seals.
Looks-1-Heritage-Tile.dc.html.Build notes: index.css :root tokens: --background #f7f3e8, --card/--popover #fffdf8, --muted #ece4d0, --muted-foreground #5e5a52, --border #d8cdb4, --input #857d6b, --primary #1a2744 / --primary-foreground #fffdf8, --accent #c8a94a, --ring #1a2744, --destructive #8a2b38, --radius 2px, plus new --gold-ink #705718 (replaces the ~135 text-lca-gold uses on light grounds; StatusBadge's #7a5c00 folds into it) and --win #2d5a45. Fonts: @fontsource/libre-caslon-display, @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4 (opsz + opsz-italic files), @fontsource/ibm-plex-mono 400/500, mapped to Tailwind fontFamily display/serif/mono (finally defining --font-mono). Components that change most: shadcn Button (navy, small caps, 2px), StatusBadge (7 word+color variants), PageHero (duotone + SVG grain, crossfade + pause instead of the auto slideshow), tournaments/StandingsTable + Crosstable (small-caps heads, hairlines, ½, color squares instead of the faint w/b), ChampionsPage/ChampionsPanel (navy honor board), Navbar/Footer (seal SVG). No new tables or endpoints.

Looks-1-Heritage-Page.dc.html.What: The shared sample page set as a printed club program: cream header with Caslon wordmark, small-caps nav and a thick–thin rule; "Lafayette Open 2026" hero with a When/Where/Format/Hosted-by ledger and a navy–cream duotone photo in a cream mat; a ruled "since 1915 · 300+ · 25+ · 7" band; Upcoming tournaments as a fixture list (date blocks, filter chips with real counts, "Partner event" tags, organizer-site note) beside "This week at the clubs" grouped by day with Tonight highlighted; Latest results as a navy honor board (gold champion row, seal, Full crosstable link); membership as four framed member cards; navy footer with Facebook kept. Collapses to one column on phones (Menu button, 2×2 stats, chips wrap, standings scroll).
Looks-1-Heritage-Page.dc.html.Borrowed from: The Masters (leaderboard-first, honor-board standings), Marshall Chess Club (history told in copy, plain interface), World Chess Hall of Fame (restraint, people photos), Pentagram's World Chess (wood/paper cues for the photo pick and mat).
Looks-1-Heritage-Page.dc.html.Trade-off: Calm and trustworthy but slow-feeling: no live state, and the duotone dulls photos that sell scholastic events; the serif-heavy header needs care at phone widths.
Looks-1-Heritage-Page.dc.html.Build notes: Same token/font swap as the tile (index.css :root + Fontsource packages); HomePage blocks map to existing data (tournaments + clearinghouse feed, clubs meeting times, champions/standings), so changes are presentational: PageHero (duotone + grain via an inline SVG filter, mat, no auto-advance), new HonorBoard variant of StandingsTable for the latest finished LCA event, a FixtureList variant of AgendaList with date blocks and FilterChips, Footer/Navbar restyle with the seal as a reusable SVG component.

Looks-2-Editorial-Tile.dc.html.What: Style tile for "Editorial Sports — results as news": Newsreader 800 headlines (proportional figures), Schibsted Grotesk for text/UI with 900-caps dark-gold kickers, Chivo Mono for agate data; white and newsprint grounds, 3px-navy-over-1px-ink rules instead of cards; status tags plus an "Upset" label; newspaper standings with a "Rtg ±" column (+24 in gain green, −3 plain ink); crosstable cells with letters + color squares; the Opera Game position before 16. Qb8+! with the queen's path in gold; ROUND 5 opener, giant-move pull quote and a pausable results ticker; natural-color tight-crop photo with credit and a slow zoom that respects reduced motion; Grand Chess Tour–style event tile (fixed 16:9 crop, Overview / Players / Results).
Looks-2-Editorial-Tile.dc.html.Borrowed from: Grand Chess Tour (fixed 16:9 event tiles linking Overview/Players/Results), Freestyle Chess (credited venue photos), The Ringer (recurring sections like "Upset of the Month"), US Chess news (the gap: a results box beside every story), ChessBase News (positions in stories, done better), The Athletic (named in the brief; not fetched).
Looks-2-Editorial-Tile.dc.html.Trade-off: Needs a volunteer to write a headline and pick a photo after every event, or it goes stale fast; three families and big type are heavier than a utility look, and the newspaper density can feel busy on phones.
Looks-2-Editorial-Tile.dc.html.Build notes: index.css :root tokens: --background/--card #ffffff, --muted #f5f4f0, --foreground #121417, --muted-foreground #5b616e, --border #e2e0da, --input #5b616e, --primary #1a2744 / #ffffff, --accent #c8a94a / #1a2744, --ring #1a2744, --destructive #c62828, --radius 2px, plus new --kicker #866a1e, --gain #1b7a43, --live #c62828. Fonts: @fontsource-variable/newsreader (opsz + opsz-italic), @fontsource-variable/schibsted-grotesk, @fontsource/chivo-mono 400/600 (sets --font-mono); Tailwind fontFamily serif/sans/mono plus a `.headline` utility with font-variant-numeric: proportional-nums. Components that change most: NewsPage/NewsPostPage (match-report layout + results box), PageHero (natural-color lead photo + credit, slow zoom off under prefers-reduced-motion), StatusBadge (+ Upset variant), StandingsTable/Crosstable (agate rows, Chivo Mono numbers, rating-change column), Navbar (masthead), new ResultsTicker (pausable) and EventTile components.

Looks-2-Editorial-Page.dc.html.What: The shared sample page as a newspaper front page: dated top strip with Donate / Log in / gold Join LCA, a centered Newsreader nameplate over the 3px-navy/1px-ink rule and a caps section nav, then a pausable results ticker (Sample data); lead story "Lafayette Open 2026" (dark-gold kicker, 86px headline, italic dek, agate When/Where/Format/Host box, Event details + Add to calendar, partner-registration note) beside a natural-color, tight-crop photo with a credit line; an index strip (since 1915 · 300+ · 25+ · 7); Upcoming tournaments as a dense calendar (weekday + mono date, Newsreader names, type column, Partner event tags, filter chips with real counts) beside a "This week at the clubs" column with Tonight highlighted; Latest results as a match report (headline, dek, byline/photo-credit placeholders, Upset and Rating movers modules) beside a newsprint Final standings box with Full crosstable; navy membership band; ruled footer with Facebook kept. On phones the photo comes first, columns stack, nav becomes Menu, tables scroll.
