Looks-2-Editorial-Page.dc.html.Borrowed from: The Athletic (front-page lead + modules; named in the brief, not fetched), The Ringer (recurring "Upset"/"Rating movers" sections), US Chess news (the missing results box beside each story), Grand Chess Tour (one fixed photo crop per event), Freestyle Chess (credited photos).
Looks-2-Editorial-Page.dc.html.Trade-off: Only as good as the last headline: with no one writing after events, the lead falls back to "next event" and the report slot goes stale; the ticker is extra motion that must stay pausable; heaviest font load of the two looks.
Looks-2-Editorial-Page.dc.html.Build notes: Bold piece is an auto-drafted match report: when a TD finalizes an LCA event, a Pages Function (functions/api/posts/draft-report) creates a draft post linked to the tournament (new posts columns tournament_id, kicker, dek, photo_credit, report_kind in D1 migration 0052), prefilled with final standings, upsets computed from pairings (win over a 200+ higher rating) and, once US Chess has rated the event, rating movers from post-event ratings via the existing uscf lookup; an officer edits the headline in admin/PostsPanel and publishes. HomePage gets a LeadStory slot (next LCA or partner event, or the newest report) and a ResultsTicker fed by /api/news/ticker (latest finished events + upsets) with pause + prefers-reduced-motion; NewsPostPage gains the results-box layout, StandingsTable a compact "box" mode, AgendaList a dense calendar variant with FilterChips; tokens/fonts as in the Editorial tile.

Looks-3-Minimal-Page.dc.html.What: The sample homepage in Modern Tech-Minimal, matched to the published tile: a sticky 92%-navy glass header with ⌘K search; a next-event hero on the 8-column a–h / 8–1 dot grid with a navy-to-gold duotone photo; events as a quiet table with "in N days"; a Mon–Sat club agenda; standings with W/D/L chips and a fixed Player column; a "Which membership fits you?" band with the family math; and a light footer with a System/Light/Dark switch.
Looks-3-Minimal-Page.dc.html.Borrowed from: Vercel's Geist design system (Geist + Geist Mono, 6/12px radii), Linear (lists as quiet tables, almost no motion), Stripe Sessions (an agenda in plain columns, used for the club week), Lichess (outcome-coloured result cells)
Looks-3-Minimal-Page.dc.html.Trade-off: The calmest and cheapest of the seven, and the most generic. Only coordinates, notation and real data make it read as chess or Louisiana, and the duotone mutes the warmth of the photos.
Looks-3-Minimal-Page.dc.html.Build notes: Map shadcn tokens in index.css: background #ffffff, foreground #0b1220, muted #f7f8fa / muted-foreground #5b6478, border #e5e7ed, input #7c8496, primary #c8a94a / primary-foreground #0b1220, accent #fbf7e9 / accent-foreground #705718 (selected chips), ring #1a2744, destructive #c0362c, plus lca-navy #1a2744, lca-gold-ink #866a1e and success #047857. Replace the stock .dark grays with #0b1220 / card #111a2c / popover #1a2744 / border white 8% / input #5f6d89 / text #e8ecf4 / muted #9aa6bf / success #3ecf8e / danger #ff6b6b, behind a System/Light/Dark switch (class on html, saved in localStorage). Use --radius 12px for cards, 6px for controls and 16px for dialogs. Fonts: fontFamily sans Geist; mono Geist Mono, which fills the undefined --font-mono so Crosstable and StandingsTable get tabular figures and ½; serif Instrument Serif italic for one accent word per page. Self-host Geist Mono 400/500 and Instrument Serif italic 400 through Fontsource, which already loads Geist; the artboard uses the equivalent single css2 link. Components: Navbar (sticky, navy/92 with backdrop blur, ⌘K CommandDialog), PageHero becomes NextEventHero, AgendaList becomes a quiet table, a new WeekAgenda reads the clubs' meeting fields, and StandingsTable gets W/D/L chips and a sticky Player column.

Looks-Compare.dc.html.What: All seven looks side by side in a 4+3 grid. Each card is set in the look's own fonts (all 21 families come from one css2 request) and shows a 5-swatch strip with hex values, a header slice with its primary "Join LCA" button, and "Registration open" / "Live · Round 3" tags in its style, plus a "Best for" line. The 8th slot explains the logo problem (today's green/yellow/purple logo next to navy and cream one-colour marks). The bottom band shows how the looks combine: one site-wide base (Tech-Minimal or Heritage Club), Broadcast Night over pairings and standings, Bright Scholastic over the Scholastic pages, and Swiss Grid or Louisiana Rooted as rebrands that would replace the base.
Looks-Compare.dc.html.Borrowed from: visual-directions.md's seven directions and their references: Pentagram's World Chess identity and Marshall Chess Club (Heritage); Grand Chess Tour and The Ringer (Editorial); Vercel Geist and Linear (Tech-Minimal); Metric's Norwegian Chess Federation identity (Swiss); The Historic New Orleans Collection and 64 Parishes (Louisiana); ONY's WSTC identity and Story Time Chess (Scholastic); Lichess broadcasts and Saint Louis Chess Club (Broadcast)
Looks-Compare.dc.html.Trade-off: Each card is a thumbnail, so subtleties such as contrast pairs, motifs and photo treatment only show on the full tiles and pages. Twenty-one families in one request is heavy, but only this board needs it. Editorial Sports gets no slot in the research's pairing, and the band says so instead of inventing a role.

Start-Principles.dc.html.What: A one-page doc on #fbfaf6. On the left are ten LCA design principles, each with a one-line rule, a concrete example and the checklist rows it maps to, followed by an 8-line "What the evidence settles" summary. On the right is ux-evidence's 39-point design review checklist, condensed into checkbox rows across 8 areas with the original numbering. Seven rows carry a red "Fails today" tag naming the current-site failure: the 5-second slideshow, colour-only status dots, the Register card below the player list on phones, no Donate entry point, gold text at 2.28:1, a focus ring at 1.54:1, and 2.1 MB of hero images.
Start-Principles.dc.html.Borrowed from: the sources behind ux-evidence.md (NN/g, Baymard, GOV.UK, USWDS, W3C WAI / WCAG 2.2), K's standing decisions (the "In 8th grade or below?" checkbox) and visual-directions' notes on 3½ and gold contrast
Start-Principles.dc.html.Trade-off: One-line rows compress some nuance, such as the mega-menu rule and the Core Web Vitals targets, so the source checklist stays the reference in a dispute. It is a static checklist, not a scoring tool. Row 17's "Fails today" tag comes from the brief's Start-Audit Fix-first list, not from the ux-evidence lines I read.

Looks-4-Swiss-Tile.dc.html.What: The style tile is itself a chessboard — files a–h run across the top and bottom, ranks 8→1 down both rails, and every block is addressed by its square ("c5 · Status"). It covers Archivo wide 800/900 + Fragment Mono, a flush 8-swatch palette strip with ratios, 0-radius flat components, a 4×2-square event card, square crosstable cells with raised opponent numbers and filled/open corner squares, Bauhaus move-shaped pieces on the Opera Game final position, and navy/paper duotone photos.
Looks-4-Swiss-Tile.dc.html.Borrowed from: Metric's Norwegian Chess Federation identity (grid + diagonal "bishop lines"), International Typographic Style, Josef Hartwig's Bauhaus chess set (piece icons), Otl Aicher's Munich 1972 (color by function → Open navy / rating-limited gold / scholastic black), Swissted (poster logic), Chess-Results and Lichess Swiss (column order, round cells).
Looks-4-Swiss-Tile.dc.html.Trade-off: The most systematic and the coldest of the seven: wide display type forces short headlines, gold can only ever be a field, and the green/yellow/purple logo has no place in it. Test it with older members before committing.
Looks-4-Swiss-Tile.dc.html.Build notes: Map onto the shadcn tokens in index.css: --background #f4f4f0, --foreground #0d0d0d, --card #fff, --primary #c8a94a with --primary-foreground #0d0d0d, --secondary #1a2744/#fff, --muted #e8e4d8 with --muted-foreground #5c5f66, --destructive #c2381f (live/alerts only), --border #0d0d0d, --ring #1a2744, --radius 0, plus --gold-700 #866a1e. Fonts come from @fontsource-variable/archivo (wdth + wght axes) and @fontsource/fragment-mono, set as --font-sans/--font-mono, with tnum on tables and liga off for notation. The biggest changes are in Button/StatusBadge (square, glyph + words), Crosstable/StandingsTable (true square cells, ½, corner-square piece color), PageHero (square duotone photo) and the header. New pieces are an EdgeCoordinates rail, a BauhausPiece icon set and section-type colors in sectionRules.ts. It implies a rebrand: the rook-Louisiana mark redrawn one-color black/navy on the grid, with the old logo kept for heritage use only.

Looks-4-Swiss-Page.dc.html.What: The homepage sample in Swiss Grid. A navy header sits over an a–h file strip, and ranks 8→1 run down the left rail as section addresses (a8 Next event, a6 Tournaments, a5 Clubs…). The type-led hero sets "Lafayette / Open 2026" in wide black at 104px over a When/Where/Type/Ages fact grid, beside a square navy/paper duotone photo. Below it: a gold stat band ("Since 1915 · 300+ · 25+ · 7"), tournament rows locked to the 8 columns with function-colored type squares and "Partner event" tags plus quick filter chips, and a Mon–Sun club week strip. The strip shows tonight in navy, real "+N more" counts, and an honest empty Sunday. Then a standings table built from true-square round cells (1/½/0, raised opponent number, open/filled corner = color) next to a navy champion block, a navy membership band and a black footer.
Looks-4-Swiss-Page.dc.html.Borrowed from: Metric's Norwegian Chess Federation identity (grid, addressed sections), Swissted (type-led poster hero), Otl Aicher's Munich 1972 (color by function), Chess-Results (column order, right-aligned ratings), Lichess Swiss (fixed-width round cells).
Looks-4-Swiss-Page.dc.html.Trade-off: It's long and rigid. The wide type and square photo add about 300px, the week strip scrolls sideways on phones, and it may feel cold to parents and older casual players.
Looks-4-Swiss-Page.dc.html.Build notes: Add a PageGrid layout (Tailwind grid-cols-8, with an EdgeCoordinates rail hidden below 900px), a duotone variant of PageHero and a ClubWeek strip. ClubWeek needs structured recurrence (day, time, "1st/3rd" rules) in a new club_meetings table or new club columns instead of free-text schedules. StandingsTable/Crosstable can render the round cells from the existing pairings data, and a Pages Function can render Swissted-style link-preview/OG images from the same layout (e.g. workers-og/satori).

Looks-5-Louisiana-Tile.dc.html.What: The style tile for "Louisiana Rooted — statewide, with an accent". Fraunces display (opsz 144, soft 100) sits over Bricolage Grotesque text and DM Mono data on magnolia paper, under a cypress top band. It shows the ironwork LCA monogram once (an open C around an interlaced L and A, after the Pontalba "AP" railings) and ten paint-chip swatches with ratios, including the catch that dark gold on moss is only 4.15, so text there uses #705718. Components: tinted 6px-corner status pills (Live is the only filled one, in brick), and a rounded event card with parish, region chip and a cypress progress bar. Chess data: standings with club chips, a parish column and muted losses, W/L/D cells, and the Opera Game on a cypress-and-moss "club vinyl" board. It closes with the region map as navigation, meander contours at full strength next to the 6% as-shipped version, and a warm-grain photo.
Looks-5-Louisiana-Tile.dc.html.Borrowed from: The Historic New Orleans Collection (mustard and dark green on cream, disciplined grid), 64 Parishes (Mardi Gras colors only inside photos; identity from specifics), Garden & Gun (serif headlines over a sans body, documentary photos), Sazerac House (gold without parade clichés), Pontalba Buildings (ironwork monogram), St. Charles streetcar line (the green), Typewolf (DM Mono paired with Fraunces).
Looks-5-Louisiana-Tile.dc.html.Trade-off: It's the warmest and most place-specific option, but kitsch is one step away. It also leans on data the site doesn't have yet (a parish for each club, event and champion). Because Fraunces has no tabular figures, the system needs three families, and the Gulf-blue "Opens" tag only just passes at 4.55.
Looks-5-Louisiana-Tile.dc.html.Build notes: Tokens: --background #fbf7ee, --foreground #1a2744, --card #fff, --muted #ebe7da with --muted-foreground #5f5b4f, --primary #2f4a3a/#fff, --accent #a4442f, --ring #1a2744, --radius 10px, plus --gulf #2c6e8f, --plum #5b2a6e, --gold-700 #866a1e, --gold-800 #705718 and --gold-300 #dec478. Fonts come from @fontsource-variable/fraunces (full axes, for SOFT/opsz), @fontsource-variable/bricolage-grotesque and @fontsource/dm-mono. The biggest changes are to PageHero (warm grain + place captions), the StatusBadge palette, StandingsTable/Crosstable (club chips via clubColors.ts, muted losses), an LCAMap restyle with a new RegionNav built on regions.ts, and the Footer. Data needs a parish on clubs and champions (D1 migration) plus a city→parish lookup for clearinghouse events. On the logo: the monogram becomes a secondary mark next to a one-color cypress/navy rook mark, and the green/purple logo can stay as heritage because plum and cypress echo it.

Looks-5-Louisiana-Page.dc.html.What: The homepage sample in Louisiana Rooted. A cypress-ruled magnolia header carries the rook mark in cypress and a Fraunces wordmark. The editorial hero sets "Lafayette Open 2026" in Fraunces with "Lafayette Parish", a South Central chip and a Partner event tag ("registration is on the organizer's site"), beside a warm-grain documentary photo with a place caption. Below it, a "since 1915 · 300+ · 25+ · 7" line sits over 6% meander contours. Tournament rows (moss date tiles, parish and region chip on every row) run beside a "Where they are" region map that filters the list. The club week splits into "Tonight · Monday" and "Later this week", with parish chips and real "+3 / +8 more" counts. Newsletter standings show club chips with club-color bars, region and muted losses, next to a champion card listed with parish. The cypress membership panel carries the page's one ironwork monogram and a gold Join button with navy type, and a moss footer has "Find chess near you" region links and Facebook.
Looks-5-Louisiana-Page.dc.html.Borrowed from: The Historic New Orleans Collection (cream, green and mustard in a disciplined grid), 64 Parishes (identity from specifics, parishes as the organizing idea), Garden & Gun (serif headlines over a sans body, documentary photos), Pontalba Buildings ironwork (monogram), St. Charles streetcar (cypress green), Chess-Results (right-aligned ratings and points).
Looks-5-Louisiana-Page.dc.html.Trade-off: It's the longest page in the set because of its newsletter spacing. The parish and region chips need data that's blank today (regions are empty, there's no parish field), so the Greater New Orleans club shows "[Parish]". The warm treatment also flattens photo contrast slightly.
Looks-5-Louisiana-Page.dc.html.Build notes: Add a parish to clubs (D1 migration: clubs.parish, and fill the empty region), plus lib/parishes.ts mapping clearinghouse cities to parish and region. Build a RegionMap filter on LCAMap/regions.ts and a "Tonight / Later this week" ClubWeek list from structured meeting times. StandingsTable gets club chips (clubColors.ts) and muted negative deltas; rating change needs post-event ratings from the US Chess upload. PageHero gets a warm-grain variant (CSS filter + inline SVG feTurbulence), and the monogram becomes an SVG component used once, in the membership band. Fonts load from Fontsource as described in the tile notes.

Looks-6-Scholastic-Tile.dc.html.What: Style tile for Bright Scholastic: Baloo 2 / Nunito / Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono on cream with navy as the anchor, one color per section (K–3 coral, K–5 mint, K–8 sky, K–12 grape), press-down buttons with a hard navy shadow, checker-strip section tabs, a pawn-to-queen sign-up track, podium medal circles, outcome-colored crosstable cells, and Morphy's Opera Game on a tournament green-and-buff board.
Looks-6-Scholastic-Tile.dc.html.Borrowed from: ONY's World Schools Team Chess Championship identity (pawn mascot, playful marks on strict type), Story Time Chess (rounded, parent-facing), ChessKid (reassure parents first), Chess in the Schools (plain big numbers), Lichess Swiss (fixed-width result cells).
Looks-6-Scholastic-Tile.dc.html.Trade-off: Five hues can tip into "toy store". It only stays credible to coaches if navy carries all text and buttons and color only ever means section, so it works as a section theme, not site-wide.
Looks-6-Scholastic-Tile.dc.html.Build notes: Scope with `[data-theme="scholastic"]` on a ScholasticLayout wrapper (ScholasticPage, scholastic event pages, RegisterPage family flow / FamilyRegistrationPanel). The wrapper overrides the shadcn vars (--background #fffaf1, --foreground and --primary-foreground #1a2744, --primary #c8a94a, --muted-foreground #4f5b75, --ring #1a2744, --radius 1rem) and adds --section-k3/k5/k8/k12 plus -tile tokens, exposed as `colors.section.*` in tailwind.config. Load fonts with Fontsource (@fontsource/baloo-2, @fontsource-variable/nunito, @fontsource/atkinson-hyperlegible-mono), imported only in the lazy scholastic route chunk, with --font-display/--font-sans/--font-mono set inside the scope. Add a `colorKey` per section in sectionRules.ts. New pieces: a `press` variant in ui/button.tsx, SectionTab, PromotionTrack (sign-up steps), MedalRank, and a CheckerStrip SVG. StandingsTable gets a medals prop and switches to cards under 640px.

Looks-6-Scholastic-Page.dc.html.What: The shared sample page in Bright Scholastic. A cream header with an app-icon mark and a four-color checker strip; a press-down hero card for the Lafayette Open with a "5 days to go" sticker and a ticket-style date; filter chips with real counts (Louisiana 11 · Scholastic 6 · Classical 3 · Dual-rated 1 · Blitz 1 · Gulf South 11); ticket-date event rows linking to the organizer's site; day cards for this week's club meetings, with Monday as "Tonight"; podium-medal standings that turn into cards on phones; and tier cards on a gold-tile band.
Looks-6-Scholastic-Page.dc.html.Borrowed from: Story Time Chess and ChessKid (friendly, parent-first tone), ONY's WSTC identity (checker strip, pawn motif), Chess in the Schools (big plain numbers), Chess-Results (right-aligned points and tiebreaks).
Looks-6-Scholastic-Page.dc.html.Trade-off: Chunky 48px+ targets and card rows make the same content about 20% taller than the 2400px plan (about 2,900px), and the playful tone fits Scholastic far better than the home page shown here.
Looks-6-Scholastic-Page.dc.html.Build notes: Uses the same `[data-theme="scholastic"]` scope as the tile. The hero is a PageHero variant fed by the next event from the clearinghouse feed, with "days to go" from lcaTime.ts. Filter-chip counts are computed client-side from the TournamentsPage query (eligibility + rating system). The club week comes from the clubs table's meeting fields (add structured weekday/time columns in a D1 migration). StandingsTable gets medals plus a card layout under 640px (pure CSS grid areas). CheckerStrip is one shared SVG component.

Looks-7-Broadcast-Tile.dc.html.What: Style tile for Broadcast Night: Barlow Condensed / Barlow / JetBrains Mono (ligatures off), with Big Shoulders Display for round banners only, on navy-black. Gold is the live accent; live red carries dark text only; elevation comes from lighter surfaces. Also shown: player bars where the gold clock marks the side to move, 4px clock bars, gold board-number boxes, outcome-colored W/L/D cells, signed rating deltas, and the Opera Game before 16.Qb8+!! with an eval bar (allowed because the game is finished).
Looks-7-Broadcast-Tile.dc.html.Borrowed from: Lichess broadcasts (LIVE and round before the title) and the lila source (shrinking 4px clock bar, fixed-width Swiss result cells; ideas only, the code is AGPL), Saint Louis Chess Club (header status line), Formula 1 results (strict time formatting), "The Great Eval Bar Debate" (restrained European tone, not esports), Norway Chess (separate stats view).
Looks-7-Broadcast-Tile.dc.html.Trade-off: Dark, condensed and data-dense is right for a dim hall or a projector but tiring for long reading. Live red is a trap (white on #ff4757 is only 3.34), so this has to stay an event-day theme, not the site default.
Looks-7-Broadcast-Tile.dc.html.Build notes: Use `[data-theme="broadcast"]` on <html> or the tournament layout, switched on automatically while an LCA-run event has a round in progress, plus a manual "Night mode" toggle remembered in localStorage. It replaces the stock shadcn `.dark` grays: --background #070b14, --card #0e1526, --popover #1a2744, --foreground #f3f5f9, --muted-foreground #8e9ab2, --primary #c8a94a / --primary-foreground #070b14, --border rgba(255,255,255,.08), --input #5f6d89, --ring #c8a94a, --radius .25rem, plus new --live #ff4757, --live-strong #c81e32, --win, --loss and --draw tokens in tailwind.config. Load fonts with Fontsource (@fontsource/barlow-condensed, @fontsource/barlow, @fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono, and @fontsource/big-shoulders-display only inside a RoundBanner), imported in the tournament route chunk, with --font-mono defined (it fixes the undefined mono in Crosstable.tsx). New PlayerBar, ClockBar, BoardNo, ResultCell, LiveBadge and ResultsTicker components. Crosstable and StandingsTable print ½ instead of .5 and show piece-color squares.

Looks-7-Broadcast-Page.dc.html.What: The shared sample page in Broadcast Night, previewed in event-day mode (labelled "Event-day preview: Sat, Oct 10, 8:15 PM" with a Night mode toggle). It has a header status line ("LIVE · R3 · Lafayette Open 2026 · Round 3 in progress · pairings posted 6:42 PM"); a live hero with Board 1 player bars and clocks, a round-progress strip and a low-key navy photo; a lower-third stat strip; a dark events table with real filter-chip counts; a TV-guide schedule of this week's club meetings; standings with outcome-colored W/L/D round cells; and a scoreboard-style membership band. All 7 blocks are kept, in order.
Looks-7-Broadcast-Page.dc.html.Borrowed from: Lichess broadcasts (LIVE and round before the title), Saint Louis Chess Club ("Open today" header status line), lila (4px clock bars, fixed-width Swiss result cells), Chess-Results (column order, right-aligned points), Formula 1 results (strict time formatting).
Looks-7-Broadcast-Page.dc.html.Trade-off: The live hero only fits event days, and this board doesn't show the non-live fallback (a countdown). Also, the Lafayette Open is a partner event, so real live data would exist only for LCA-run events or partners using LCA's pairing engine. It's taller than planned (about 2,850px) because of the dense tables.
Looks-7-Broadcast-Page.dc.html.Build notes: The page flips `data-theme="broadcast"` when any LCA-run event has a round in progress, via a small Pages Function `GET /api/tournaments/live` (reads round state and pairings-posted time from D1; polled every 30–60s, or SSE later). The status line and Board 1 bars read existing pairings/results (TournamentPairingsPage data, with clocks only if the TD enters them; otherwise hide them). Round progress comes from the event's round schedule. The events table becomes stacked rows under 760px. StandingsTable gets round cells, and Rk + name are sticky while rounds scroll on phones. The theme toggle is persisted per viewer in localStorage.

Nav-Header.dc.html.What: Five full-width desktop headers on real pages, each with one state open — H1 Refined (six visible sections, click-open About menu showing "You are here", fixed Donate · Log in · Join LCA), H2 Two-tier (thin live bar: "Lafayette Open · Round 3 pairings posted · Find your board", plus a chip row of the line's other states), H3 Mega menu (Tournaments panel: find, next 3 real events, results/records incl. Scanner, "Run a tournament" box), H4 Search-in-header (typed "bat" → grouped tournaments / clubs / players suggestions; sections drop to a white second row), H5 Event mode (gold strip: Live · Round 3, 7:00 PM countdown, "My board: 6 · White", Pairings, Standings, round-alert bell, hide-for-today). Board header lists changes from today (Scanner out of the main bar, Membership out of More, Donate added, admin links into My LCA, Facebook kept).
Nav-Header.dc.html.Borrowed from: NN/g (visible nav beats hamburger, click-not-hover submenus with carets, show current location, utility nav top-right, visible search box +91%), USWDS (dropdown up to 6 links, mega menu above that, 0.5 s hover delay), WCAG 3.2.6 consistent help order.
Nav-Header.dc.html.Trade-off: H2 and H5 only pay off if pairings are actually published on the site during events; H4 adds a search index to maintain for a ~40-page site where list filters may be enough; H3 is the heaviest to keep accessible (focus trap, Esc, keyboard order).
Nav-Header.dc.html.Build notes: Rewrite Navbar.tsx around six fixed sections + utility (Donate, Log in → "My LCA" menu holding role-gated Workspace/Admin from roles.ts, Join LCA) using shadcn NavigationMenu (click-open, delayDuration 500 for H3); H2/H5 read a new GET /api/live Pages Function (current LCA event, round, pairings_published_at, next round start; edge-cached 30 s) plus GET /api/me/live-board for the signed-in player's board/color, with alerts via Web Push (push_subscriptions table, VAPID) and Resend fallback; H4 needs GET /api/search?q= backed by a D1 FTS5 table over tournaments, clubs, posts and players from published crosstables (scholastic players excluded), refreshed on write.

Nav-Mobile.dc.html.What: Four 390 px phone navs — M1 Combo bar (LCA mark + always-visible "Tournaments" + bordered "Menu" button; open sheet with the current section expanded as "You are here", Scoresheet scanner under Tournaments, then Donate · Log in · Join LCA and Facebook/Contact/Help), M2 Bottom tab bar (Events · Clubs · My LCA with a to-do count · Menu, over an Events list with quick chips, "38 of 60 registered" and partner events that register on the organizer's site), M3 Full-screen task tiles on navy (Find a tournament "11 coming up", Find a club "Tonight: 6 clubs meet", Get my child playing, Results and standings, Join or renew "From $5 a year", Donate, plus all six sections), M4 Event-day mode (in-page "Round 3 pairings are posted" banner and a persistent "Pairings · Round 3 · Board 6 · White" pill floating over any page).
Nav-Mobile.dc.html.Borrowed from: NN/g (combo nav used 86% vs 57% for hidden menus; labelled, bordered Menu button; show current location), GOV.UK (task-based rather than audience-based entry points), ux-evidence §1 (event-day "Pairings" shortcut).
Nav-Mobile.dc.html.Trade-off: M2's tab bar spends 72 px on every screen and its "Events" label differs from the desktop "Tournaments"; M3 hides everything behind one tap; M4 depends on pairings being published on the site and on players being logged in.
Nav-Mobile.dc.html.Build notes: New MobileNav (shadcn Sheet) or BottomTabs component replacing the Navbar hamburger below lg; tile sublines and the My LCA count from a new GET /api/home-summary (tonight's meetings, upcoming-event count) and /api/me (unpaid renewals, pending registrations); M4 = EventPill component that polls GET /api/live (or SSE) every 30 s and shows only when /api/me/live-board returns a board, with round-ready alerts via Web Push (push_subscriptions table, VAPID keys, sent from the pairings-publish handler) and a Resend email fallback.

Nav-Footer.dc.html.What: Three complete footers — F1 Refined navy four columns (Play incl. Scoresheet scanner / Community incl. Facebook / About LCA / Contact with LouisianaChess@gmail.com) beside a brand block with Join LCA + Donate, and an affiliate base line; F2 Doors (gold "Join LCA" with real dues, "Find a club" with tonight's real meetings, Donate, "Volunteer as a TD", then a one-line sitemap); F3 light Trust footer ("Who runs LCA": US Chess state affiliate, since 1915, elected volunteer board, minutes in the open · "Talk to a person" inbox + website help ticket + Facebook · "The Monday digest" signup with region and scholastic-only options · a computed freshness line: site last updated, clearinghouse sync, club schedule confirmations).
Nav-Footer.dc.html.Borrowed from: federations research (NC and England four-column footers with governance links and an affiliate line), Stanford credibility guidelines and NN/g social proof ("reviewed recently", a real contact), NN/g utility-nav consistency.
Nav-Footer.dc.html.Trade-off: F2's doors repeat calls to action already in the header and homepage; F3's freshness line backfires if the numbers look stale (it needs clubs to actually confirm), and the digest adds an email list LCA must manage (consent, unsubscribes).
Nav-Footer.dc.html.Build notes: Footer.tsx with a variant prop; F2 door lines from GET /api/home-summary (tonight's meetings, dues from the membership tiers in pricing.ts); F3 needs a digest_subscribers table (email, region, scholastic_only, confirmed_at, unsubscribe_token) with double opt-in through Resend, a Monday send in the existing daily-emails Worker cron built from tournaments + club schedules, and GET /api/site-status (max updated_at across content tables, clearinghouse last_sync_at, count of clubs with schedule_confirmed_at in 90 days); new static Privacy and Accessibility pages.

Home-C.dc.html.What: The homepage is a living weekly agenda: a navy hero with the identity line and a computed summary ("Mon, Oct 5 – Sun, Oct 11 · 19 club meetings at 15 clubs · Lafayette Open Sat–Sun · National Chess Day"), last/this/next week switcher, region chips and "Near me"; then a Mon–Sun strip of every real club meeting with today's column wider ("Tonight", happening-now tag, a club-rep cancellation, Picayune's 1st-Monday quick-rated night) and the Lafayette Open in the Sat/Sun columns; then "This weekend" (registration card with "38 of 60 registered" plus partner events that register on the organizer's site), "Coming up · next 6 weeks" grouped by week (real Louisiana and Gulf South events plus club specials), a side rail with latest results, a public "No meeting time on file" list for 7 clubs and a Monday-email / calendar-feed signup, then the join band with real dues and the 300+ members stat.
Home-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: clubs-brands top ideas #1–2 ("Tonight / This week" strip and a statewide weekly grid), NN/g homepage guidance (say who you are, show real dated content, no carousel), Stanford credibility ("reviewed recently"), NC-style clickable quick filters.
Home-C.dc.html.Trade-off: The page is only as good as club schedules, so a stale or missing schedule shows in public on the front page; newcomers get less storytelling (no photo hero, no news lead), and the grid is dense on phones, where it becomes one long day-by-day list.
Home-C.dc.html.Build notes: Replace free-text club schedules with a club_meetings table (club_id, recurrence rule such as weekly Mon or monthly 1st/3rd Tue, start/end time, venue, notes, rated flag) plus meeting_exceptions (date, cancelled, note, posted_by) and clubs.schedule_confirmed_at; new GET /api/week?start=&region= Pages Function expands rules and merges tournaments (LCA + clearinghouse) into days; WeekStrip, TonightColumn and ComingUpList components on HomePage; one-tap "Cancel this meeting" in ManageClubPage; an iCal feed at /api/calendar.ics?region= and the Monday digest (Resend, daily-emails Worker cron) reuse the same endpoint; monthly "is this still right?" nudges to club reps keep it fresh.

Home-F.dc.html.What: Map-first homepage: an identity line + "Chess near you, anywhere in Louisiana" with a City/ZIP field and "Use my location"; a statewide map beside a synced "Near you" list (all 25 real clubs as pins, clusters for New Orleans Metro "8" and Baton Rouge "2", rings on the 6 clubs meeting tonight, gold squares for the 3 tournaments in the next 30 days, layer chips + This week / Next 30 days / All upcoming, South Central Louisiana selected with its 5 clubs and 2 tournaments, Lafayette Open popover with "38 of 60 registered"); clickable stats (25+ clubs, 7 regions, 11 upcoming Louisiana events, 300+ members, 110+ years); upcoming Louisiana events with region and "On the map"; "Tonight at the clubs" with counts for the rest of the week; "Explore by region" cards (clubs, meets tonight, next tournament or "Host one", board seat placeholder) plus a "List a club" card; a cream join band with real dues.
Home-F.dc.html.Borrowed from: Baymard (95% used a map placed beside the list vs 65% who never found it on list-only sites), NC federation (clickable stats), NN/g homepage guidance (identity line, real dated content), LCA's own LCAMap (navy/gold pins).
Home-F.dc.html.Trade-off: The map hero pushes event details below the first screen, so it serves "what's near me" better than "register for this weekend"; region data is blank in the live site today, and a map is harder to make fully accessible than a list (the list stays the primary, keyboard-usable path).
Home-F.dc.html.Build notes: GET /api/map?layers=clubs,events&window=30d Pages Function returning lat/lng, region, meets_tonight and next event per pin (from clubs, the club_meetings schedule rules and tournaments + clearinghouse); a statewide SVG map component for the hero (no API cost) with LCAMap (Google Maps JS + @googlemaps/markerclusterer) on zoom or on ClubsPage; migration to backfill clubs.region by point-in-polygon against parish-based region outlines in regions.ts, then a club-rep confirm step in ManageClubPage; "Use my location" uses the browser Geolocation API and sorts client-side (never sent); stats and region cards from GET /api/home-summary; region cards read board seats (BoardSeatsPanel data) for the representative name or "Seat vacant".

Home-Phones.dc.html.What: Home options A, B, C and E at 390 px under one combo-nav app header (visible "Tournaments" link plus a labelled Menu): A = Lafayette Open hero with an inset of its event-day live state; B = type-ahead search with results grouped by type plus stat links; C = Mon–Sun strip of the 19 real meetings with tonight first and "On now"; E = the three doors as a one-open-at-a-time accordion.
Home-Phones.dc.html.Borrowed from: NN/g (combo nav beats hidden menus), ChessRoster and Marshall/Columbia/Norway (new-round banner, live mode), Saint Louis "OPEN TODAY" and Melbourne's weekday list (tonight strip), RA and Luma (agenda with day headings), Charlotte's branching idea (three doors, without its lead-capture form).
Home-Phones.dc.html.Trade-off: A spends the first screen on one event (strong when an LCA event is near, thin between events); B only feels instant with a real index behind it; C is only as good as the clubs' structured times; E costs one extra tap before content.
Home-Phones.dc.html.Build notes: New shared MobileHeader (combo nav); HomePage hero from `GET /api/tournaments/next` switching to a live state from published pairings (poll 60 s, "Updated" from published_at); `GET /api/search?q=` Pages Function over D1 tournaments, clubs and regions (regions.ts) plus the existing uscf lookup, grouped by type; new `club_meetings` table (club_id, weekday, start/end, week-of-month rule, confirmed_at) evaluated with lcaTime.ts for "Tonight/On now"; doors are links with URL params into TournamentsPage, ClubsPage and ScholasticPage.

Tourn-Phones.dc.html.What: The tournaments list on a phone in four states: a month-grouped agenda with a Louisiana chip applied (removable, "11 events", Subscribe); a near-full-height filter sheet (When / Where with state counts and a region row / Type / Where you register / rated-only) whose button shows the live total "Show 16 events"; a Monday-first month grid with event bars that jumps the agenda below; and one row expanded in place with sections, fees, spots left, Register, Add to calendar and Share.
Tourn-Phones.dc.html.Borrowed from: Baymard and AllTrails (filter panel with an Apply button and live count, removable applied chips), RA and Luma (agenda with day headings and a count line), AskFRED, USATF and Luma (row with "X of 60 registered" and separate Register/Details), Luma and USATF (Subscribe / add to calendar), FIDE's calendar (switchable list/calendar views).
Tourn-Phones.dc.html.Trade-off: The sheet covers the list while you choose (the live count compensates). The Monday-first grid breaks the US Sunday-first habit to keep weekend events on one line. Expanding rows in place makes the list long, so only one stays open at a time.
Tourn-Phones.dc.html.Build notes: TournamentsPage mobile: new FilterSheet (reuse the DirectorsModal mobile bottom-sheet pattern) with filter state in URL params and facet counts from `GET /api/tournaments?…&facets=1` (state, region via regions.ts, type, source = LCA or clearinghouse.ts); MiniCalendar rebuilt Monday-first with multi-day bars (lcaTime.ts); AgendaList rows become accordions that read sections and fees from sectionRules.ts/pricing.ts and live entry counts; `/api/tournaments.ics` feed for Subscribe.

Event-Phones.dc.html.What: The event page on a phone with a sticky bottom Register bar in three states ("$40 early · Register · $40", then "Registered · Change section or byes"), the top of the 2027 Paul Morphy Open above the fold (weekday dates, plain-language G/90+30, 38 of 60, early/regular/late ladder), sections and fees with a "Which section fits me?" lookup that marks and reorders eligible sections, a live "Who's coming" list with section chips and "Updated 2 min ago", and the real Mississippi State Championship partner listing whose bar opens the organizer's site.
Event-Phones.dc.html.Borrowed from: Luma, Meetup and Dice (one action button whose state changes: Register / Registered / Join waitlist / Closed), Baymard and Meetup (change section or byes without withdrawing and re-registering), AskFRED, USATF and Luma ("X of 60 registered"), Eventbrite ("Good to know" and the round schedule as their own sections, here as in-page tabs).
Event-Phones.dc.html.Trade-off: A fixed bar permanently takes about 90 px of a small screen and has to be kept out of the way of the in-page tabs. Listing young players by first name and last initial departs from full-name entry lists some players expect. The partner page can only show what the feed carries (no sections, fees or status).
Event-Phones.dc.html.Build notes: TournamentDetailPage: new StickyRegisterBar (position fixed, safe-area padding) driven by pricing.ts (current tier, member price) and the viewer's registration (Register · price / Registered · Manage / Join waitlist / Closed); sticky in-page tabs with IntersectionObserver; "Which section fits me?" reuses UscfSearchInput plus sectionRules.ts eligibility; `GET /api/tournaments/:id/entries` (rating-sorted, section counts, name display from the existing grade-8-or-below eligibility flag) polled every 60 s; the partner page renders clearinghouse.ts fields plus a stored synced_at, with "Report a problem" filing a support ticket.

Clubs-Phones.dc.html.What: The clubs directory on a phone in four states: a list sorted by next meeting where each row leads with when ("On now · until 5:00 PM", "Tonight 5:30 PM"), with "Confirmed Sep 2026 · Report outdated info" and a floating Map button; a zoomed southeast-Louisiana map with clustered pins, "Search this area" and a bottom sheet whose card is linked to the gold selected pin (Houma); the week as swipeable day columns holding every real meeting, tonight first; and a filter sheet (days, time of day, region or Near me, kind of club, opt-in "no listed schedule") with a live "Show 8 clubs".
Clubs-Phones.dc.html.Borrowed from: Airbnb (linked pins), Yelp ("Search this area" and the list/map toggle), Baymard (map findability on list-first sites; filter panel with a live count, with AllTrails), USA Swimming and AllTrails (suitability filters such as kids' programs and rated games), Saint Louis "OPEN TODAY" and Melbourne's weekday list (this-week view).
Clubs-Phones.dc.html.Trade-off: Sorting by next meeting needs every club's schedule as structured data (7 clubs have none and drop to the end). Day columns show only about two days at a time, so a statewide glance needs swipes. Clustered pins hide individual clubs until you zoom.
Clubs-Phones.dc.html.Build notes: ClubsPage mobile: list/map view state in URL params; LCAMap gains a selectedClubId shared with the sheet, marker clustering (@googlemaps/markerclusterer) and a bounds-changed "Search this area" query; bottom sheet with snap points; new `club_meetings` table (weekday, start/end, week-of-month rule) plus `confirmed_at` on clubs, evaluated with lcaTime.ts for next meeting and "On now"; "Report outdated info" files a support ticket and emails the club rep via Resend; `GET /api/clubs?…&count=1` for the live count.

Schol-Phones.dc.html.What: Scholastic for parents on phones at the venue: a live day view of the (real) New Orleans Youth Chess November Meet showing each family child's board and colour, the round in progress on a timeline (check-in to awards, later times marked as estimates), "Updated 1 min ago" and an opt-in round-ready alert; a per-child "What to bring" checklist saved to the family account, plus a plain-English glossary accordion; "Find a youth program" with the real youth programs, honest "Schedule not listed" and "LCA lists these programs; it doesn't vet or certify them"; and upcoming scholastic events with the Grand Prix series as one line and partner events sent to the organizer.
Schol-Phones.dc.html.Borrowed from: AskFRED (first-tournament guide with a glossary and a day-of checklist), ChessRoster ("Round 3 pairings are ready" banner) and Marshall, Columbia and Norway (live mode), Luma (what to bring and reminders before the day), parkrun (first-visit logistics box), ChessKid (plain parent-trust language), Little League and USA Swimming (program finders by place and kind), Luma, Meetup and Dice ("Opens … remind me" state).
Schol-Phones.dc.html.Trade-off: The live view only works for LCA-run events where pairings come out of LCA's own engine, not for partner meets. Alerts need push permission (iOS only for home-screen web apps), so email is the fallback. The program finder is only as current as the programs keep it.
Schol-Phones.dc.html.Build notes: Live day view for LCA-run scholastic events: `GET /api/me/live` returns, per family member (family.ts), the current round, board, colour and last result from the pairing engine, polled every 60 s; round-ready alerts via Web Push (VAPID keys, `push_subscriptions` table) with a Resend email fallback, fired when a TD publishes pairings; a per-event `schedule` JSON (time, label, is_estimate); `family_checklists` rows per child and event; youth programs = clubs with a `program_types` tag set; a `series_id` on tournaments for the Grand Prix line.

Schol-B.dc.html.What: A five-rung staircase (club night → first scholastic meet → NOLA Youth Chess Grand Prix → LCA State Scholastic → Nationals) whose rungs list real upcoming events, then live Grand Prix standings by grade band with team standings and follow-a-player alerts, auto-awarded milestones, and the "Send a Louisiana kid to Nationals" fund with a live total.
Schol-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: pathway ladder with "qualified via" (FIDE Candidates); series leaderboard (Downriver youth page, Grand Chess Tour standings); stepping stones before rated opens (US Squash); kid-sized milestones (parkrun junior); follow + reminders (Luma, Strava); named fund with progress bar (US Chess Women, Saint Louis's Sponsor a Student, Berkeley's Building Fund).
Schol-B.dc.html.Trade-off: The Grand Prix meets are partner-run, so automatic points only work if organizers run meets in LCA's TD tools or upload final standings; public kids' standings and the scoring rules need organizer and parent sign-off.
Schol-B.dc.html.Build notes: New D1 tables series, series_events (tournament_id or clearinghouse event id), series_results (player_key, band, score) with a computed standings view, plus follows (user, player_key, alert prefs) and a donations.fund column carried in Stripe metadata; endpoints GET /api/series/:id/standings, POST /api/series/:id/import (CSV or US Chess report via uschessUpload.ts), GET /api/donations/fund/:slug; new PathwayLadder, SeriesStandings, FollowButton, Milestones (on FamilyCard) and FundProgress components on ScholasticPage; alerts ride the daily-emails Worker; a family-level name-display flag (initial / hidden).

Schol-C.dc.html.What: A scholastic hub with an audience switch and three doors (Parents, Coaches, Schools), one merged table of real scholastic events (LCA vs partner sign-up, iCal subscription), a map-based youth program finder over the 5 youth programs plus 3 kid-friendly clubs, a coach team-entry workflow with per-section eligibility checkboxes and a school-invoice option, a host-an-event request, and the State Scholastic honor roll.
Schol-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: audience row (Ireland); parent page order (England Football); "For parents" as a hub (NN/g); first-year discount (England, Ireland) and private entry-fee help (NC); safeguarding link (Ireland, US Chess, Norway); coaches roster (old LCA Google Site); eligibility checkbox instead of birthdate (AskFRED); compact coming-up rows (NC).
Schol-C.dc.html.Trade-off: It is a long page that tries to serve three audiences at once, and team entry adds a new coach role, parent-confirmation emails and invoice handling for volunteers to support.
Schol-C.dc.html.Build notes: New D1 tables teams (school/club, coach user), team_players (name, US Chess ID, parent_email, confirmed_at; no grade/DOB) and youth_programs (or a clubs.type/program_tags column) plus host_requests routed into BoardInboxPage; endpoints POST /api/registrations/team (one Stripe checkout or an invoice record), GET /api/calendar/scholastic.ics (Pages Function merging tournaments + clearinghouse rows), POST /api/board/host-request; reuse UscfSearchInput, GradeConfirm (per-section wording), FamilyRegistrationPanel patterns and LCAMap with program filters; new ScholasticHub, TeamEntryPanel and ProgramFinder components; a coach capability added in roles.ts.

News-C.dc.html.What: News as five labelled sections (Results, Announcements, From the clubs, Scholastic, Board updates), each a short dated list of 3–4 rows with its own "See all", "In my digest" toggle and RSS, under a pinned announcement; the side rail holds a build-your-digest form (sections + clubs + weekly/monthly), the Facebook rail with links back to Facebook, and a club-rep posting prompt.
News-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: one block per tag with "Show more" (Ghost Headline); short grouped teasers ending in "See all" (Harvard design system); rows rather than cards plus "Load more" (NN/g); newsletter archive (Colorado, Texas, Marshall); plain-language meeting summary (Councilmatic).
News-C.dc.html.Trade-off: Five sections need steady posting; a thin section (Board updates) looks stale fast, and auto-posted results read flat until someone writes the recap.
News-C.dc.html.Build notes: Add posts.section (results/announcement/club/scholastic/board) and posts.source (manual/auto), and switch the club_news feed back on; finalizing standings in TournamentManagePage creates an auto results post; new digest_subscriptions (email or user, sections, club_ids, frequency) table sent by the daily-emails Worker through Resend; Pages Functions GET /api/news?section=&cursor= and /api/news/:section/rss.xml; NewsPage rebuilt from new NewsSection + NewsRow components, FacebookFeed moved to the side rail, PostsPanel gains a section picker.

News-D.dc.html.What: A recap article template for every LCA event: a TD-only draft bar (filled in from final standings), headline, byline and fact chips, hero photo and lede, a winner card per section, an Open standings snippet with round-by-round results, a key-game diagram with replay controls and a Lichess link (Opera Game final position as the stand-in, checked square by square), a photo grid with the Facebook album link and a same-day take-down promise, quotes, and a rail with event facts, follow-a-player, the share preview and "Up next".
News-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: bylined recap with section winners, ratings, top-board games and rating-report link (Central Florida Chess Club); one-sentence results summary (parkrun); 14:10 share images (Substack); event pages with Games and Photos (Grand Chess Tour, FIDE Candidates); follow with reminders (Luma, Strava).
News-D.dc.html.Trade-off: Auto-drafts make recaps cheap but tempt publishing tables with bracketed gaps; someone still has to write the story and pick the game, and photos of kids need a consent and take-down routine.
News-D.dc.html.Build notes: Finalizing standings (TournamentManagePage) triggers a Pages Function that creates a draft posts row (section=results, tournament_id) prefilled from StandingsTable/PrizeWinners data; posts gains tournament_id, key_game_pgn and R2 photo keys; new RecapTemplate, WinnersGrid and GameViewer (PGN replay, Lichess import link, fed by ScannerPage output) components on NewsPostPage; player pages need a players table keyed by US Chess ID with result history; follows table shared with Schol-B; an OG Pages Function for /news/:slug injects meta tags and renders the share image (satori + resvg-wasm).

About-B.dc.html.What: A board page built around "who do I call": a "Who represents me?" lookup (club, city or ZIP) that routes a message to the right rep and falls back to the whole board when the seat is open; officer cards with role, term, one-line duties and Message; a numbered Louisiana map showing seat status (filled navy disc vs dashed gold ring, plus words) beside seven region rows built from live clubs and next events (shared seat shown); and open seats as "This seat is open — interested?" invitations with a short job description and an interest form that lands in the board inbox.
About-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: board as two groups with open seats labeled (Michigan, Texas); regional directors list (Texas); board cards with seat and term (USA Ultimate); contact and support first (NN/g, Mozilla); election timing on governance pages (Florida, Southern California).
About-B.dc.html.Trade-off: Empty seats and "none listed yet" for quiet regions become very visible, and the lookup only works once clubs have confirmed regions (blank in live data today).
About-B.dc.html.Build notes: Board seat records (BoardSeatsPanel) gain region, term_end and duties (shared holders already supported); clubs.region gets filled through a confirm step on ManageClubPage plus a ZIP/city-to-region table in regions.ts; new GET /api/board/lookup?q= (club/city/ZIP → seat → contact slug or board inbox) and POST /api/board/interest (a BoardInboxPage item tagged with the seat, optionally auto-posting to News as section=board); BoardPage rebuilt with RegionMap (inline SVG, not Google Maps), RegionRow and SeatInterestForm, reusing /contact?to=slug routing.

Tourn-B.dc.html.What: Master–detail list. A compact, month-grouped list (16 events) drives a sticky preview pane with the facts, sections and fees, live per-section counts, household checkout and Register (or "Register on organizer site"). The selected event is kept in the URL. Below it, three more pane states: partner event, entries not open yet (Notify me), and the shared-link preview.
Tourn-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: NN/g (side panel instead of a pop-up; lists over cards for comparing), Luma (status slot plus "N going", which becomes "X of Y registered"), Resident Advisor (dated rows with an attending count), North Carolina Chess Association (an internal page for every clearinghouse event with "Register on organizer site"), Baymard (removable applied-filter chips with a count).
Tourn-B.dc.html.Trade-off: the two panes need about 1200px. On tablets and phones the layout falls back to list, then a full-screen sheet, so "preview without losing your place" only works on desktop. The pane also gets long for LCA events.
Tourn-B.dc.html.Build notes: TournamentsPage gets a `?event=` param and a new PreviewPane that merges LCADetailPane and ExternalDetailPane, fed by GET /api/tournaments/:id/summary (per-section counts from registrations, member and early prices from pricing.ts). It embeds FamilyRegistrationPanel for a single Stripe Checkout per household and RegistrationReminderButton for events not yet open. A Pages Function serves per-event OG tags plus a generated OG image (live count drawn in, cached in R2). It also needs J/K/Enter/Esc key handling and a full-screen sheet on mobile.

Tourn-C.dc.html.What: The rebuilt calendar works as a navigator. A 9-month season strip (counts split into LCA and partner) and a clean Monday-first month grid sit beside a week-grouped agenda. In the grid, Sat–Sun events draw as one bar, today is marked, deadline and "entries open" ticks show, and a gold frame marks the week in view. The agenda opens with one featured next event. A Club nights layer adds the real weekly meetings ("Tonight: 6 club meetings", including Picayune's quick-rated first Monday), and a per-filter .ics subscription keeps phones in sync.
Tourn-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: Hund, Dowell & Mueller 2014 (a list beats a grid across month breaks, so the grid only navigates), Luma (small month grid with dots beside the list, plus Subscribe), USA Pickleball (each day labelled with a count), lichess (monthly calendar plus subscribed feeds), USATF and Luma (iCal subscribe / add to calendar).
Tourn-C.dc.html.Trade-off: the two views must stay in sync (scroll-spy moves the grid frame, and tapping a day scrolls the list). Big weekends get busy (Oct 24 stacks three bars). On phones the grid stacks above the list and the side-by-side navigation is lost. Club nights are only as accurate as clubs keep their schedules.
Tourn-C.dc.html.Build notes: replace the MiniCalendar + AgendaList [260px 1fr 300px] grid with new SeasonStrip and MonthGrid components (Monday-first, bars laid out per week) plus scroll-spy on AgendaList. Deadline ticks come from the existing pricing.ts early/late dates plus new reg_opens_at / online_close_at fields. Club nights need a new club_meetings table (club_id, weekday, nth_weeks, start_time, note) seeded from the club map data. A Pages Function GET /cal/events.ics?src=&region=&add= serves RFC 5545 output (stable UID, DTSTAMP, DTSTART), with webcal and Google "add by URL" links.

Tourn-D.dc.html.What: Split map view. On the left, a list sorted by estimated drive time from a typed city or ZIP (or "Use my location"). On the right, a Gulf South map: filled pins for LCA events, hollow pins for partner events, clusters, and 100/200/300-mile rings. Pins beyond the chosen drive time fade, and the selected event gets an anchored card with Register. Under the map, Louisiana region counts show the gaps (none in North or Central LA), and a radius alert ("email me when something is posted within 4 hours") turns the view into a standing subscription.
Tourn-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: Baymard (split view, map beside the list, never in a pop-up), US Chess tournament search (distance from a ZIP code), FIDE calendar (tiles / table / map switch), AskFRED (distance filter), USA Swimming (results show distance), Little League (honest "distances are approximate"), Luma (separate map view), NN/g (ask for location only on request, with a reason).
Tourn-D.dc.html.Trade-off: drive times need geocoding plus a routing API and caching, and they are still estimates. Houston and the Jackson area cluster at state zoom. On phones the map stacks above the list and eats the screen. With most near-term events in the south of the state, the map mostly confirms how little there is up north.
Tourn-D.dc.html.Build notes: reuse maps/LCAMap (Google Maps JS) with event markers and marker clustering in place of the static SVG. Geocode LCA tournaments and clearinghouse listings on save and sync (new lat/lng columns; the clearinghouse sync Worker geocodes). Drive times come from the Google Distance Matrix API, cached per origin ZIP and event in D1 or KV. A new tournament_alerts table (email, origin_zip, max_minutes, include_partner, unsubscribe_token) is checked by the daily-emails Worker cron and sent through Resend. Region counts use regions.ts plus a region field on events.

Tourn-E.dc.html.What: A dense, sortable power table of all 25 upcoming events. Date and Event are frozen; the other columns are City · Type · Rating · Sections · Entries/cap (with mini bars) · Status (with the next deadline) · Source. Saved views sit in a tab bar, each with email alerts, its own .ics feed and a shareable URL. There's a column chooser, compact/comfortable density, CSV export and checkbox batch actions ("Add 3 to my calendar"). Rows expand in place to show sections, fees and live counts, plus Manage, Check-in and Pairings on the director's own events. A director-facing date-clash checker charts weekend load within driving range and suggests open Saturdays that link straight into the wizard.
Tourn-E.dc.html.Borrowed from: NAChessHub (dense list columns: date · state · city · type · rating · time control · organizer), Tabroom ("Closed" / "Due 10/5" deadlines in the list), AskFRED (rows expand into a table; "Download as CSV"), NN/g (fixed header, frozen first column, checkbox batch actions), Chesstide (chosen columns are remembered), FIDE calendar (table view), Baymard (filters kept in the URL).
Tourn-E.dc.html.Trade-off: it's intimidating for newcomers and parents, so it belongs behind the view switch, not as the default. It also exposes how thin the partner listings are ("Not listed", "Not in feed"), because the feed carries no sections, fees or status. The clash checker depends on the same drive-time data as the map.
Tourn-E.dc.html.Build notes: new saved_views table (user_id, name, query_json, alert_mode, ics_token) with GET/POST/DELETE /api/me/views. Build the table on a headless table library (e.g. TanStack Table) with sticky columns and per-user column and density prefs. Add a GET /cal/v/:token.ics Pages Function, plus a multi-event .ics for batch "add to calendar". The daily-emails Worker cron matches view alerts and sends them through Resend. Add GET /api/tournaments/clash?date=&origin=&max_minutes= over tournaments and clearinghouse events (sharing Tourn-D's drive-time cache), with "Start an event" pre-filling admin/TournamentWizard. Row expansion reuses Tourn-B's event summary endpoint.

Work-B.dc.html.What: Club rep workspace (Houma Chess Club) built around the freshness loop: "Is this still accurate?" with one-tap confirm and visitor reports, a Tonight switch (on / moved / cancelled → club page + follower email), a structured-schedule club page editor with live card preview, club news with "Suggest for LCA News", tournament creation behind LCA review, and a members table with renewal reminders and QR club-night sign-in.
Work-B.dc.html.Borrowed from: NC ("Last confirmed" stamp + "Report outdated info"), England Football (clubs manage their own listing), Luma and RA (submit an event → approval queue), parkrun (meeting time as the headline, first-visit box), Linear ("What's new" for reps), NN/g data tables; NOLA Chess Club's stale site as the cautionary case.
Work-B.dc.html.Trade-off: A lot for a volunteer who logs in twice a year (the emailed one-tap check and the Tonight switch have to carry it), and showing members' renewal status to reps needs an explicit privacy rule; board is 200px taller than planned.
Work-B.dc.html.Build notes: D1 adds club_meetings (weekday, start, end, pattern), clubs.last_confirmed_at + first-visit fields, club_reports (escalate_at → admin queue), club_followers, club_meeting_overrides (date, moved/cancelled, note), club_checkins (QR); signed one-tap confirm links from the daily-emails Worker; endpoints in functions/api/clubs (confirm, reports, overrides, followers, members) and posts (suggest_to_lca → approvals). ManageClubPage becomes tabbed (Overview/Club page/Tonight/News/Tournaments/Members), reusing AdminClubPage's hex picker + R2 logo upload, ClubLocationPicker and RichTextEditor; roles.ts gives club_rep tournament-create, and TournamentWizard saves club events as pending_review.

Work-C.dc.html.What: Admin home at /admin with K's grouped sidebar (queues first) and one merged "Needs attention" queue — approvals, support tickets, board inbox, failed emails and club-listing gaps — where every row has an owner, waiting time and its own action button; count tiles filter it, and the page also holds a self-expiring site banner, an automations health panel, the audit log and a "Log in as" that asks for a reason.
Work-C.dc.html.Borrowed from: Luma and Strava (approval queues; Luma's "pending approval by the calendar admin"), NN/g (data tables with the readable name first and batch-style filters; never show an error only as a toast), Linear-style weekday digest of open work.
Work-C.dc.html.Trade-off: The merged queue needs one item model across five existing systems and someone who actually owns assignment; with two or three admins the owner column may go unused. Board is 150px taller than planned.
Work-C.dc.html.Build notes: D1 admin_queue_items (source, source_id, title, owner_id, created_at, resolved_at) fed by support, board inbox, approvals (tournaments pending_review, posts suggested_to_lca, club_rep_requests), Resend bounce/complaint webhooks and clubs missing meetings; job_runs (job, ran_at, status, counts) written by the clearinghouse sync Worker, daily-emails cron, Stripe webhook and Facebook refresh; banners gain starts_at/ends_at/audience; impersonation requires a reason and logs actor + subject. Endpoints functions/api/admin/{queue, queue/:id/assign, jobs, banner, impersonate}. AdminPage becomes a sidebar shell that hosts AdminSupportPage, BoardInboxPage, AdminEmailPage, AdminAnnouncementPanel, AuditLogPanel, MembersTable/MembersExportMenu, BoardSeatsPanel, ChampionsPanel and PostsPanel; a "/" jump box searches members, tournaments, clubs and tickets; the 7:00 AM digest rides the daily-emails Worker; ImpersonationBanner blocks Stripe checkout.

Work-D.dc.html.What: One-page setup checklist for an LCA event (Paul Morphy Open 2027, cloned from 2026) with quick-add section presets (Open/U1800/U1400/U1000 or K–12/K–8/K–5/K–3, plus a Morphy Scholastic side event), a fee-ladder timeline with member discount, a schedule check that flags tight turnarounds for G/90+30, bye and lapsed-membership rules, registration settings (cap, waitlist with 24 h claim, "X of 120 registered", family checkout), and a right rail with the checklist, live event-card preview, a server-rendered link-preview card and scheduled publish (news, follower email, banner); club reps get "Submit for LCA review".
Work-D.dc.html.Borrowed from: ChessRoster, Chesstide and onlineregistration.cc (resumable checklist, quick-add section chips, fee tiers, bye rules, import previous tournament), Chess67 ("finish setting up" checklist, per-event warn/email/block for lapsed memberships, and its "Loading…" link previews as the counterexample), pickleball.com (schedule-problem warnings), KingRegistration (plain server-rendered pages).
Work-D.dc.html.Trade-off: Every step on one page is fast for experienced TDs but less guided than a one-step-at-a-time wizard for a first-time club rep; the schedule check and the dynamic preview image are extra moving parts.
Work-D.dc.html.Build notes: Turn TournamentWizard into this checklist page over a tournaments draft row (status draft/pending_review/scheduled/published, publish_at, source_tournament_id) plus functions/api/tournaments/:id/clone (dates +1 year); SectionRulesEditor gains preset chips and the yes/no eligibility flag; pricing.ts gets a per-section early/regular/late ladder + member discount; new lib scheduleCheck.ts (time control → longest game → gap warnings); Pages Functions functions/t/[slug].ts (OG/Twitter meta) and functions/og/[slug].png (workers-og or Satori + resvg-wasm) with the live registered count, short cache; publish hooks write a posts row, queue a region-follower Resend email and an optional banner; the club_rep path lands in the admin approval queue.

Scan-A.dc.html.What: Desktop review screen for the scanner: scoresheet photo on the left (the move being checked is highlighted on the sheet), a scoresheet-style move list in the centre that labels "fixed automatically" (7. Qb3, read as Qb8) apart from "you checked" (9...b5) and "check this" (13...Rxd7), and a board on the right at the exact selected position with ranked candidates that say why the others fail ("15. Scan-A.dc.html.Borrowed from: Chess67 (photo and moves side by side, threefold-repetition flag, one-tap export), lichess (import for analysis; broadcast board grid for the TD view), Ireland's results rows that link to each game, Chess-Results / AskFRED / IRLchess (PGN downloads).
